missouri-working-family-tax-credit: Missouri's Working Family Tax Credit is a state earned income tax credit equal to 20 percent of your federal Earned Income Tax Credit for tax year 2024 and forward. It is nonrefundable, so it lowers the Missouri tax you owe but cannot go below zero, and it cannot be carried forward to a later year. Claim it on your Missouri income tax return.
medical-assistance-medicaid-and-minnesot: Medical Assistance is Minnesota's Medicaid program, free or low-cost health coverage for children, pregnant people, parents, adults, older adults, and people who are blind or have a disability. MinnesotaCare covers many people whose income is a little too high for Medical Assistance, for a low monthly premium. Apply through MNsure at mnsure.org, or reach DHS Health Care Consumer Support at 1-800-657-3672.
indiana-legal-services-free-civil-legal-: Indiana Legal Services is the statewide nonprofit law firm that gives free civil legal help to low-income residents on housing and eviction, family, public benefits, consumer, and other noncriminal matters. Apply online at indianalegalservices.org, or apply by phone at 1-844-243-8570, Monday through Thursday, 10am to 2pm Eastern.
tanf-cash-help: Monthly cash payments for very-low-income Texas families with children 18 and younger, paid on the Lone Star Card. One-Time TANF also gives a single crisis payment, and certain relatives raising a child can get a once-in-a-lifetime $1,000 payment.
family-employment-program-utah-cash-assi: The Family Employment Program, FEP, is Utah's monthly cash assistance for low-income families with children, run by the Department of Workforce Services. It pairs the cash with an employment plan and one-on-one help from a case manager to move you toward work. Apply online through myCase at jobs.utah.gov/mycase. State and federal time limits apply to how long you can receive cash.
low-income-energy-assistance-program-lie: LIEAP pays part of your heating bill once a year. The money goes straight to your heat company, not to you. People age 60 or older and disabled people getting DAAS services apply in December. Everyone else applies starting in January, until money runs out or March 31.
missouri-snap-food-stamps: SNAP is Missouri's food stamp program: monthly food money on an EBT card you use like a debit card at most grocery stores. Apply online any time through myDSS at mydss.mo.gov, run by the Family Support Division, or ask for a paper application. The FSD Information Center is 1-855-373-4636 (1-855-FSD-INFO), Monday through Friday, 8am to 5pm.
indiana-medicaid-hoosier-healthwise-and-: Indiana Medicaid is free or low-cost health coverage. Hoosier Healthwise covers children and pregnant people, and the Healthy Indiana Plan, HIP, covers low-income adults ages 19 to 64. Apply online through the FSSA Benefits Portal at fssabenefits.in.gov, or by phone at 1-800-403-0864. For help with HIP enrollment, call 877-GET-HIP-9, which is 1-877-438-4479.
pa-211: Dial 2-1-1 from any Pennsylvania phone, or text your zip code to 898-211, for free, confidential help finding local assistance: housing, utilities, food, childcare, and more. PA 211 covers all 67 counties around the clock through regional United Way centers.
snap-food-assistance-access-florida: Florida SNAP puts monthly grocery money on an EBT card that swipes like a debit card. One MyACCESS application at myaccess.myflfamilies.com can start SNAP, cash assistance, and Medicaid together.
weatherization-assistance-program-florid: Free home energy improvements for income-qualified Florida households so future utility bills shrink. FloridaCommerce funds local weatherization agencies statewide; apply through the office that serves your county.
florida-medicaid: Free or low-cost health coverage for low-income Florida children, pregnant women, parents, seniors, and people with disabilities. SSI recipients are enrolled automatically; everyone else applies through MyACCESS.
minnesota-211-united-way: Dial 2-1-1 from any Minnesota phone, or call 1-800-543-7709, for free, confidential help finding local assistance with housing, utility bills, food, healthcare, and more. Minnesota 211, run by United Way, answers around the clock, every day, in many languages. You can also text your zip code to 898-211 or search at 211unitedway.org.
new-jersey-earned-income-tax-credit: The New Jersey Earned Income Tax Credit, NJEITC, is worth 40 percent of your federal EITC and is refundable, so it can put cash back in your pocket even if you owe no state tax. New Jersey does not follow the federal age limits: residents at least 18 by year end can claim it, with or without children. File a New Jersey Resident Income Tax Return, the NJ-1040, to claim it.
weatherization-assistance-program-nebras: Free home energy-efficiency work for income-eligible Nebraska households: insulation, air sealing, heating-system safety checks, and repairs that lower future bills. The Nebraska Department of Water, Energy, and Environment runs the program through eight nonprofit community action agencies. Contact the provider serving your area to apply. Call 1-877-253-2603 or 402-471-2186 for help finding yours.
alaska-legal-services-corporation: Alaska Legal Services Corporation provides free civil legal help to low-income Alaskans on housing, family, consumer, public benefits, health care, and Alaska Native law matters. Call the statewide intake line at 1-888-478-2572 to reach the office serving your area, or apply online at alsc-law.org/intake. Offices are open Monday through Friday, 9am to 5pm.
weatherization-assistance-program-north-: Free home energy-efficiency work for income-eligible North Dakota households: insulation, air sealing, and heating-system improvements that lower future bills and make the home safer. North Dakota's Community Action Agencies have weatherized homes since 1976, and both homeowners and renters can qualify. There is no fee for applicants. Call 1-800-726-7960 or contact the Community Action Agency serving your area to apply.
wyoming-kid-care-chip: Kid Care CHIP is low-cost health coverage for children of working parents who earn too much for Medicaid. It covers check-ups, immunizations, prescriptions, dental, vision, and mental health care, with preventive and dental care free and other services at a small co-pay. Apply through the same WES portal at wesystem.wyo.gov, or call 1-855-294-2127. One application checks a child for both Medicaid and CHIP.
connecticut-wic: WIC gives healthy food, breastfeeding support, nutrition education, and health referrals to pregnant and postpartum people, infants, and children up to age 5. Connecticut WIC runs through local agencies of the state Department of Public Health. Start online with the WIC interest form, or call the state WIC office at 1-800-741-2142 to find your local clinic.
usagov-benefit-finder: Official government screening tool that checks 1,000+ federal and state programs you may qualify for in about 10 minutes.
unemployment-insurance-arkansas: Temporary weekly payments if you lost work through no fault of your own, from the Arkansas Division of Workforce Services. File your first claim online through EZARC at ezarc.adws.arkansas.gov, then file weekly certifications through Arkansas LAUNCH at launch.arkansas.gov. For help, call the UI Service Center at 1-844-908-2178, Monday through Friday, 8am to 4pm.
wyoming-lieap-low-income-energy-assistan: LIEAP helps low-income Wyoming households pay winter heating bills. Wyoming takes applications online only, through the Utility Assistance portal, generally from October 1 through April 30 each heating season. For the current window and help applying, call 1-800-246-4221 or email lieapinfo@wyo.gov. Approved LIEAP applicants are automatically considered for free weatherization work.
delaware-medicaid: Delaware Medicaid is free or low-cost health coverage for children, pregnant people, parents, older adults, people with disabilities, and low-income adults. Delaware expanded Medicaid, so low-income adults ages 19 to 64 can qualify on income alone. Apply online through Delaware ASSIST at assist.dhss.delaware.gov, or call the Division of Medicaid and Medical Assistance at 302-255-9040.
michigan-home-heating-credit: The Home Heating Credit is a refundable Michigan tax credit that helps low-income residents pay winter heating costs. You can claim it even if you are not required to file a state income tax return, and you do not have to owe tax to get it. File form MI-1040CR-7 by September 30.
new-mexico-medicaid-turquoise-care: New Mexico Medicaid is free or low-cost health coverage for children, pregnant people, parents, older adults, people with disabilities, and low-income adults. Most members get care through Turquoise Care, the managed care program that replaced Centennial Care on July 1, 2024. Apply online through YESNM at yes.nm.gov, or call the Consolidated Customer Service Center at 1-800-283-4465.
indiana-energy-assistance-program-eap-li: The Energy Assistance Program, Indiana's LIHEAP, helps low-income households with winter heating and summer cooling costs, paid straight to your utility. It runs through the Indiana Housing and Community Development Authority and local service providers. Applications open for the heating season each fall and typically close in mid-April. Find the provider serving your county through IHCDA or by dialing 2-1-1.
maryland-snap-food-supplement-program: SNAP is Maryland's Food Supplement Program: monthly food money loaded onto an EBT card you use like a debit card at most grocery stores. Apply online through MarylandBenefits at MarylandBenefits.gov, which also handles Medicaid, cash assistance, and energy help on one account, or at your local department of social services. You can also call the DHS Customer Call Center at 1-800-332-6347, Monday through Friday, 8:30am to 5pm.
minnesota-snap-food-support: SNAP, still called Food Support by many Minnesota counties, puts monthly food money on an EBT card you use like a debit card at most grocery stores and many farmers markets. Apply online at mnbenefits.mn.gov, the state's one application that also covers cash and other help, or file a paper Combined Application Form (DHS-5223) at your county or Tribal human services office. A SNAP outreach specialist through MNFoodHelper (mn.gov/dhs/mnfoodhelper) can help you apply for free.
idaho-grocery-credit: Idaho's grocery credit refunds part of the sales tax you pay on groceries, generally $155 per person for the year, or up to $250 per person if you save your food receipts. You claim it on your Idaho income tax return, and residents who are not required to file can still claim the refund using Form 24. Idaho has no state Earned Income Tax Credit, so this is the main state tax refund working families should not miss.
west-virginia-211: Dial 2-1-1 from any West Virginia phone, or call 1-833-848-9905, for free, confidential help finding local assistance with housing, utilities, food, healthcare, and more. West Virginia 211 answers 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, every day of the year. You can also text your zip code to 898-211 or search at search.wv211.org.
work-first-new-jersey-cash-assistance: Work First New Jersey, WFNJ, is the state's cash assistance program. WFNJ/TANF serves families with children, and WFNJ/General Assistance serves single adults and couples without children. It pays monthly cash and adds child care, job help, and short-term housing support. Apply at njhelps.gov or your county board of social services.
oklahoma-wic: The Oklahoma Women, Infants and Children program, WIC, gives healthy food, breastfeeding support, nutrition education, and health referrals to pregnant and postpartum people, infants, and children up to age 5. Apply through the online WIC enrollment tool or a local WIC clinic. For more information, call 1-888-655-2942 or 405-426-8500.
heap-energy-assistance-ohio: Ohio's Home Energy Assistance Program is a one-time benefit applied to your heating or cooling bill, plus a Winter Crisis Program (November 1 to March 31) and a Summer Crisis Program for emergencies. As of April 2026 it is run by the Ohio Department of Job and Family Services. Apply online, by appointment, or by mail through your local Energy Assistance Provider.
211-wisconsin: Dial 2-1-1 from any Wisconsin phone, or call 1-877-947-2211, for free, confidential help finding local assistance with housing, utilities, food, healthcare, and more. 211 Wisconsin answers around the clock, every day, and connects you to programs near you. You can also search at 211wisconsin.communityos.org.
wyoming-power-cash-assistance-tanf: POWER, Personal Opportunities With Employment Responsibilities, is Wyoming's version of TANF: monthly cash assistance for low-income families with children, paired with a work program. There is also a Caretaker Relative track for relatives raising a child whose parents are absent. Download the Application for Assistance and contact your local Department of Family Services office to set up an appointment. For program questions call 307-473-3948.
medi-cal-kern-county-dhs: Free or low-cost health insurance covering medical, dental, and vision care. You may qualify even if you work, own a home or car, or are not a U.S. citizen.
colorado-legal-services: Colorado Legal Services provides free civil legal help to low-income and older Colorado residents on housing, family, public benefits, consumer, and other noncriminal matters. Call the intake line at 303-837-1313 to reach the office serving your area, or apply online at coloradolegalservices.org. Free plain-language legal information and self-help forms are at lawhelp.colorado.gov.
alaska-heating-assistance-program-hap-li: The Heating Assistance Program, HAP, is Alaska's LIHEAP: a one-time seasonal payment sent straight to your heating vendor as a credit on your account. The heating season runs October 1 through April 30, and the deadline for regular, non-crisis help is April 30. Apply through the Alaska Connect portal or a local Public Assistance office, or call 800-478-7778.
north-dakota-wic: WIC gives healthy food, breastfeeding support, nutrition guidance, and health referrals to pregnant and postpartum people, infants, and children up to age 5. To start, call the statewide toll-free line at 1-800-472-2286, schedule online at signupwic.com, or call your local WIC clinic. The first appointment is in person and takes about 30 to 45 minutes.
legal-services-alabama: Legal Services Alabama provides free civil legal help to low-income residents on the noncriminal problems that upend a household: eviction and housing, domestic violence, public benefits, consumer and debt issues, and more. Apply online at legalservicesalabama.org, or call the statewide intake line at 1-866-456-4995, Monday through Friday, 8:30am to 4:30pm.
florida-211-network: Dial 2-1-1 anywhere in Florida for free, confidential, 24/7 help finding local assistance: food, housing, utility bill help, health care, and crisis support. Eleven accredited centers cover all 67 counties.
colorado-wic: WIC gives healthy food, breastfeeding support, nutrition education, and health referrals to pregnant and postpartum people, infants, and children up to age 5. Colorado WIC runs through local clinics. Start by filling out the online referral form at coloradowic.gov and a staff member contacts you within 10 days, or call your local WIC clinic directly. The state WIC office line is 303-692-2400.
kansas-earned-income-tax-credit: Kansas has a refundable state Earned Income Tax Credit worth 17 percent of your federal EITC. Because it is refundable, it can pay out as cash even when it is larger than the Kansas tax you owe. Claim it on your Kansas income tax return (Form K-40). You generally must qualify for the federal Earned Income Tax Credit first.
washington-basic-food-snap: Basic Food is Washington's name for SNAP: monthly food money on an EBT card you use like a debit card at most grocery stores. Apply online at washingtonconnection.org, which handles Basic Food, cash assistance, and other help on one application, or by phone at 1-877-501-2233, Monday through Friday. You can also apply at your local DSHS Community Services Office.
legal-aid-of-west-virginia: Legal Aid of West Virginia gives free civil legal help to low-income residents on housing and eviction, family law, public benefits, consumer and debt problems, and more. Call the statewide intake line at 1-866-255-4370 to reach the office serving your area, or apply for help online at legalaidwv.org. This is civil, noncriminal help.
colorado-earned-income-tax-credit: Colorado's Earned Income Tax Credit is a refundable credit worth a percentage of your federal EITC, so it can pay out as cash even if you owe no state tax. For tax year 2025 it equals 50 percent of your federal EITC. For tax year 2026 the rate drops to 25 percent. Claim it on your Colorado income tax return.
weatherization-assistance-program-north-: Free home energy-efficiency work for income-eligible North Carolinians: insulation, air sealing, and heating and cooling repairs that lower future bills. The NC Department of Environmental Quality runs it through local agencies. Use the Find Your Agency tool on the DEQ site to reach the provider serving your county.
mississippi-211: Dial 2-1-1 for free, confidential help finding local Mississippi assistance with housing, utilities, food, and healthcare. If 2-1-1 does not connect from your phone, search your zip code at 211.org to reach the resource center that covers your area. It is available around the clock.
snap-food-benefits-new-york: New York SNAP puts monthly grocery money on an EBT card. Check eligibility and apply at myBenefits.ny.gov, or through your local department of social services. Questions go to the OTDA toll-free hotline at 1-800-342-3009.
delaware-earned-income-tax-credit: Delaware offers two versions of the Earned Income Tax Credit, and you pick the one that helps most. One is refundable and equal to 4.5 percent of your federal EITC, so it can pay out even if you owe no tax. The other is nonrefundable and equal to 20 percent of your federal EITC, which can wipe out more tax but cannot drop below zero. Claim it on your Delaware return using DE Schedule II.
montana-tanf-cash-assistance: Temporary Assistance for Needy Families, TANF, is Montana's monthly cash assistance for low-income families with children. Most adults take part in TANF Pathways, the work program run for the state by Maximus, which helps you move toward a job. Apply online at apply.mt.gov, in person at your local Office of Public Assistance, or by phone at 1-888-706-1535.
oklahoma-earned-income-tax-credit: Oklahoma has a state Earned Income Tax Credit worth 5 percent of your federal EITC. As of tax year 2022 the Oklahoma credit is refundable again, so it can pay out as cash even when it is larger than the state tax you owe. Claim it on your Oklahoma income tax return.
montana-snap-food-assistance: SNAP is Montana's food assistance program: monthly food money on an EBT card you use like a debit card at most grocery stores. Apply online at apply.mt.gov, which also covers Medicaid and TANF cash on one application, in person at your local Office of Public Assistance, or by phone through the Public Assistance Helpline at 1-888-706-1535.
omni-family-health: A network of health centers in Kern County providing medical, dental, and behavioral health care with a sliding fee scale if you are uninsured or money is tight. Call or text to make an appointment.
liheap-energy-assistance-alabama: The Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program helps low-income Alabama households pay home heating and cooling costs, and it can step in during an energy crisis such as a shutoff. The Alabama Department of Economic and Community Affairs funds LIHEAP but does not take applications; you apply through the community action agency serving your county. Find your agency through ADECA, or dial 2-1-1.
iowa-energy-assistance-liheap: Iowa's Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program, LIHEAP, helps qualifying households pay part of their winter heating costs. You apply at your local community action agency, not online, and each agency serves a set of counties. Applications open October 1 for households with a member age 60 or older or with a disability, November 1 for everyone else, and close April 30.
weatherization-assistance-program-dc: Free home energy-efficiency work for income-eligible District households: energy audits, insulation, duct sealing, and heating and cooling repairs that lower future bills. DOEE runs the program through local nonprofit contractors. Openings are delayed this fiscal year, and DOEE contacts waitlisted applicants first. Apply online, or email your application to energyefficiency.conservation@dc.gov, and reach the Residential Service Line at (202) 299-3316, Monday through Friday, 8:30am to 2:30pm.
virginia-snap-food-assistance: SNAP is Virginia's food assistance program: monthly food money on an EBT card you use like a debit card at most grocery stores. Apply online through CommonHelp at commonhelp.virginia.gov, which handles SNAP, Medicaid, TANF, and energy assistance on one application, or at your local department of social services. You can also apply by phone at 1-855-635-4370.
virginia-tanf-cash-assistance: Temporary Assistance for Needy Families, TANF, is Virginia's monthly cash assistance for low-income families with children. Most adults take part in the Virginia Initiative for Education and Work, VIEW, which helps you move toward a job. Apply online through CommonHelp at commonhelp.virginia.gov or at your local department of social services.
ri-works-cash-assistance: RI Works is Rhode Island's cash assistance and employment program for parents and families with little to no income who have children high school age or younger. It pairs a monthly cash payment with job readiness, training, and child care support, and kinship guardians such as grandparents raising a child can apply too. Apply online through the HealthyRhode portal at healthyrhode.ri.gov or by phone through the DHS Call Center at 1-855-697-4347.
north-carolina-wic: WIC gives healthy food, breastfeeding support, nutrition education, and health referrals to pregnant and postpartum women, infants, and children up to age 5. NC WIC is offered statewide through county health departments and community health centers. Call 1-844-601-6881 to find your local WIC clinic.
utah-heat-home-energy-assistance: HEAT is Utah's home energy assistance program, the state's version of LIHEAP, helping low-income households with heating and other home energy costs. Priority households, those with someone age 60 or older, a person with a disability, or a child under 6, can apply starting October 1, and the general public can apply starting November 1, running through September 30 or until federal funds run out. Contact your local HEAT office or call 801-526-9240.
iowa-snap-food-assistance: SNAP is Iowa's food assistance program: monthly food money loaded onto an EBT card you use like a debit card at most grocery stores. Apply online through Iowa's HHS Services Portal at hhsservices.iowa.gov, which handles SNAP, FIP cash, and Medicaid on one application, or at your local Iowa HHS office. You can also apply by mail or ask questions at 1-800-972-2017.
iowa-legal-aid: Iowa Legal Aid provides free civil legal help to low-income Iowans on housing, family, public benefits, consumer, and other noncriminal matters. Call the statewide intake line at 1-800-532-1503 if you are under 60, open Monday through Friday, 9 to 11am and 1:30 to 3:30pm and closed Thursday afternoon. Iowans 60 and older have a separate line at 1-800-992-8161.
kidscare-arizona-chip: KidsCare is Arizona's Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP), run by AHCCCS: low-cost health coverage for children under 19 whose family earns too much for regular AHCCCS but still needs affordable coverage. KidsCare monthly premiums are paused until further notice. Apply online through Health-e-Arizona Plus at healthearizonaplus.gov.
connecticut-energy-assistance-program-ce: The Connecticut Energy Assistance Program, CEAP, is the state's LIHEAP: help with winter heating bills for income-eligible households, with payments usually made straight to your utility or fuel dealer. The Department of Social Services runs it through nine regional Community Action Agencies. To apply, dial 2-1-1 to be connected to the agency serving your town. For the 2025-2026 heating season, applications opened September 1, 2025 and run through May 29, 2026.
wisconsin-works-w-2-cash-assistance: Wisconsin Works, called W-2, is the state's TANF program: monthly cash assistance and employment services for parents of minor children and pregnant women with low income. The Department of Children and Families runs it through local W-2 agencies, and most participants take part in work activities. Apply online through ACCESS at access.wisconsin.gov or at your local W-2 agency.
unemployment-insurance-nevada-detr: Temporary weekly payments if you lost work through no fault of your own, from the Nevada Department of Employment, Training and Rehabilitation, DETR. File online at ui.nv.gov, which is the fastest way and open around the clock. You file an initial claim, then a claim for each week to keep payments coming, and you must stay able, available, and looking for work while you claim.
new-hampshire-emergency-assistance-housi: Emergency Assistance, EA, helps New Hampshire families with children facing a housing or utility crisis: homelessness, a utility shutoff, or no heat, hot water, or cooking fuel. It can pay a rental security deposit or first month's rent, back rent, utility deposits or arrears, or a home heating fuel delivery. Families must meet the FANF eligibility rules but do not have to receive the cash benefit. Apply through your local DHHS District Office, or call 1-844-275-3447.
americas-job-center-of-kern: Free job search help, resume workshops, training programs, and computer access at 1600 E. Belle Terrace in Bakersfield. A youth center serves job seekers ages 18 to 24.
ohio-211: Dial 2-1-1 from any Ohio phone for free, confidential help finding local assistance: housing, utilities, food, healthcare, and mental health. Ohio 211 runs through regional United Way hubs, and a 2026 statewide expansion is extending around-the-clock coverage toward all 88 counties.
louisiana-wic: WIC gives healthy food, breastfeeding support, nutrition education, and health referrals to pregnant and postpartum people, infants, and children up to age 5. Louisiana WIC runs through local health units and clinics. Find your clinic and start an application at louisianawic.org, or call 1-800-251-2229 (1-800-251-BABY).
weatherization-assistance-program-connec: Free home energy-efficiency work for income-eligible Connecticut households: insulation, air sealing, and heating-system improvements that lower future bills. The Department of Energy and Environmental Protection runs the Weatherization Assistance Program through local Community Action Agencies. Contact the Community Action Agency serving your area to apply, and note that applying for energy assistance generally screens you for weatherization too.
massachusetts-legal-aid-masslegalhelp-ma: Massachusetts legal aid programs provide free civil legal help to low-income residents on eviction, housing, family, public benefits, consumer, and other noncriminal matters. Find free plain-language legal information at masslegalhelp.org, and use the Massachusetts Legal Resource Finder at masslrf.org to see whether you qualify for a legal aid program that serves your city or town.
michigan-legal-help: Michigan Legal Help is a free website with plain-language legal information and do-it-yourself tools that build court forms for people without a lawyer. It covers eviction, family law, debt, and public benefits, and points you to legal aid and self-help centers across the state. The tools and information are free to everyone.
utah-snap-food-assistance: SNAP is Utah's food assistance program: monthly food money loaded onto an EBT card you use like a debit card at most grocery stores. The easiest way to apply is online through myCase at jobs.utah.gov/mycase, the state's one application for food, medical, financial, and child care assistance. You can also apply at a Department of Workforce Services employment center or by calling 1-866-435-7414.
peachcare-for-kids: Georgia's CHIP: affordable health coverage for uninsured children up to age 18 whose families earn too much for Medicaid. DCH now charges no premiums for PeachCare; small copays of $0.50 to $12.50 apply for some services.
weatherization-assistance-program-indian: Free home energy-efficiency work for income-eligible Indiana households: insulation, air sealing, and heating-system improvements that lower future bills. The Indiana Housing and Community Development Authority runs the program through local service providers. IHCDA does not take applications directly, so contact the provider serving your area to apply. To find your provider, dial 2-1-1.
nevada-tanf-cash-assistance: Temporary Assistance for Needy Families, TANF, is Nevada's monthly cash assistance for low-income families with children. It comes with work requirements that help you move toward a job, and it carries a 60-month lifetime limit on how long an adult can receive benefits. Apply online through Access Nevada at accessnevada.nv.gov or at a local Division of Welfare and Supportive Services office. Call 775-684-0800 with questions.
edd-unemployment-and-disability-insuranc: Unemployment benefits if you lost work, State Disability Insurance if you can't work due to illness/injury, and Paid Family Leave.
arkansas-211: Dial 2-1-1 for free, confidential help finding local assistance with food, housing, rent, utilities, and childcare. Arkansas 211 is run by Hark at the Excellerate Foundation and currently answers calls from Benton, Madison, and Washington counties in Northwest Arkansas, with service expanding. You can also call 1-866-489-6983 around the clock, or text your zip code to 898211.
nevada-snap-food-assistance: SNAP is Nevada's food assistance program: monthly food money on an EBT card you use like a debit card at most grocery stores. The fastest way in is Access Nevada at accessnevada.nv.gov, the state's online portal that also handles Medicaid, cash assistance, and energy help. You can also apply at a local Division of Welfare and Supportive Services office or by phone at 775-684-0800. Households with almost no money can get benefits within 7 business days.
unemployment-insurance-rhode-island: Temporary weekly payments if you lost work through no fault of your own, from the RI Department of Labor and Training. File online through UI Online at uionline.dlt.ri.gov, which is the fastest way, or call the call center at 401-415-6772. The call center is open Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday from 8am to 3pm, Friday from 9:30am to 3pm, and is closed Wednesday.
palawhelp-org-eviction-and-legal-help: Free, plain-language legal information for Pennsylvanians and a directory of the legal aid programs that serve each county, from the Pennsylvania Legal Aid Network. Covers eviction, benefits, family law, and more, with a Legal Help Finder to reach a local provider.
hawaii-general-assistance-ga: General Assistance (GA) is Hawaii's state cash program for adults ages 18 through 64 who have little or no income, do not have minor children, are temporarily disabled, and do not qualify for federal aid like Social Security. A DHS medical board must certify that you cannot work at least 30 hours a week for at least 60 days. Apply through the Department of Human Services, and call the Public Assistance Information Line at 1-855-643-1643 for information.
washington-apple-health-medicaid: Apple Health is Washington's Medicaid program: free or low-cost health coverage for children, pregnant people, parents, older adults, people with disabilities, and low-income adults. Apply online at wahealthplanfinder.org, or call the Washington Healthplanfinder Customer Support Center at 1-855-923-4633. For coverage questions, the Health Care Authority line is 1-800-562-3022.
weatherization-assistance-program-west-v: Free home energy-efficiency work for income-eligible West Virginia households: insulation, air sealing, and heating-system improvements that lower future bills. The work is delivered by local Community Action agencies. Call the West Virginia Community Action Partnership at 304-347-2277 or use its agency locator to reach the weatherization provider serving your county, since you apply through that local agency.
new-york-state-earned-income-credit: A refundable state tax credit for low- and moderate-income workers, worth 30 percent of your federal Earned Income Tax Credit, reduced by any New York household credit. Because it's refundable, you can get money back even if you owe no state tax. Claim it by filing a state return with Form IT-215.
kentucky-legal-aid-civil-legal-help: Kentucky has four regional civil legal aid programs that give free legal help to low-income residents on housing, family, public benefits, consumer, and other noncriminal problems. Which office serves you depends on where you live: Kentucky Legal Aid in the south and west, Legal Aid Society around Louisville, Legal Aid of the Bluegrass in the north, and AppalReD Legal Aid in eastern Kentucky. Find your program and free self-help legal information at kyjustice.org.
calfresh-california-snap: California's food benefits program — monthly money on an EBT card for groceries. Apply through BenefitsCal, the state's official benefits site, or call 1-877-847-3663. (GetCalFresh no longer takes applications.)
the-mission-at-kern-county: Overnight shelter, three hot meals a day, showers, and laundry at 816 East 21st Street in Bakersfield, every day of the year. Also offers recovery programs and support for women with children.
minnesota-working-family-credit: The Working Family Credit is Minnesota's version of the Earned Income Tax Credit, a refundable credit for workers with low income. It equals 4 percent of your earned income, up to a maximum of $379, and it can pay out even if you owe no tax. You claim it on Schedule M1CWFC with your Minnesota return, the same form that carries the state Child Tax Credit.
legal-aid-dc: Legal Aid DC, the Legal Aid Society of the District of Columbia, provides free civil legal help to low-income residents on housing and eviction, family and domestic violence, public benefits, and consumer and debt matters. Call the intake line at (202) 628-1161, or apply online at legalaiddc.org/help. Intake hours are limited to certain days, so check the site before you call.
covered-california: California's health insurance marketplace with income-based subsidies if you earn too much for Medi-Cal.
home-weatherization-assistance-program-o: Free home energy-efficiency work for income-eligible Ohioans: insulation, air-leak sealing, and heating-system repairs that lower future bills. HWAP runs through local energy assistance providers serving all 88 counties, and as of April 2026 is administered by the Ohio Department of Job and Family Services.
unemployment-insurance-wyoming: Temporary weekly payments if you lost work through no fault of your own, run by the Wyoming Department of Workforce Services. File online through the WYUI portal at wyui.wyo.gov, which is the fastest way, or reach the Claims Center at 307-473-3789, open 8am to 4pm Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, and Friday, and 8am to noon Wednesday.
weatherization-assistance-program-wiscon: Free home energy-efficiency work for income-eligible Wisconsin households: insulation, air sealing, and heating-system improvements that lower future bills. The Division of Energy, Housing and Community Resources runs the program through local agencies. Apply online at energybenefit.wi.gov or through your local agency, and call the Customer Care Center at 1-800-506-5596 with questions.
healthy-texas-women: Free women's health services for uninsured Texas women 15 to 44: annual exams, family planning, and screenings and treatment for conditions like diabetes and high blood pressure. Use the site's Find a Doctor tool to locate a provider.
snap-food-stamps: Monthly benefits on an EBT card to buy groceries. The largest food assistance program in the country — millions of eligible people never apply.
2-1-1-texas: Texas's statewide helpline for finding local assistance of every kind: rent, utility bills, food, shelter, and healthcare. Run by Texas Health and Human Services; dial 2-1-1 or call the toll-free line, with help in English and Spanish.
unemployment-insurance-montana: Temporary weekly payments if you lost work through no fault of your own, from the Montana Department of Labor and Industry. File online through the claimant portal at uiclaimant.mt.gov, then request payment each week you are unemployed. For help, call the Claims Processing Center at 406-444-2545.
2-1-1-in-georgia-united-way-network: Dial 2-1-1 from any Georgia phone for free, confidential help finding local assistance: food, housing, utility bills, health care, and more. Regional United Way centers answer for their own service areas across the state.
utah-wic: WIC gives healthy food, breastfeeding support, nutrition education, and health referrals to pregnant and postpartum people, infants, and children up to age 5. To apply, call or text your local WIC clinic to set up an appointment. For general information call 801-273-2991, or find your clinic and how to apply at wic.utah.gov.
rhode-island-earned-income-credit: Rhode Island's Earned Income Credit is a refundable credit worth 16 percent of your federal Earned Income Tax Credit for tax years 2024 and 2025, up from 15 percent in earlier years. Because it is refundable, it can pay out as cash even when it is larger than the tax you owe. Claim it on your Rhode Island income tax return; you generally must qualify for the federal EITC first.
603-legal-aid-free-civil-legal-help-in-n: 603 Legal Aid runs New Hampshire's statewide intake for free civil legal help on noncriminal problems: eviction and housing, family, public benefits, consumer, and debt matters for low-income residents. Call the intake line at 1-800-639-5290 (or 603-224-3333), open 9am to 12:30pm, Monday through Wednesday. It works alongside New Hampshire Legal Assistance to serve the whole state.
montana-211: Dial 2-1-1 from any Montana phone for free, confidential help finding local assistance with housing, utilities, food, healthcare, and more. Montana 211 is a statewide service run by regional United Way partners, and it answers around the clock, every day. You can also search at montana211.org.
connecticut-earned-income-tax-credit: Connecticut offers a refundable state Earned Income Tax Credit worth 40 percent of your federal EITC. Because it is refundable, it pays out as a refund even when it is larger than the state tax you owe. Claim it on your Connecticut income tax return using Schedule CT-EITC.
nebraska-snap-food-assistance: SNAP is Nebraska's food assistance program: monthly food money on an EBT card you use like a debit card at most grocery stores. Apply online through iServe Nebraska at iserve.nebraska.gov, the state's one application for SNAP, ADC cash, Medicaid, energy help, and child care. You can also apply at your local DHHS office or call DHHS at 402-471-3121.
unemployment-insurance-colorado: Temporary weekly payments if you lost work through no fault of your own, from the Colorado Department of Labor and Employment. File your claim online through MyUI+ at cdle.colorado.gov, which is the fastest way, or call the customer support center at 1-800-388-5515 or 303-318-9000, Monday through Friday, 8am to 4pm.
delaware-snap-food-supplement-program: SNAP, called the Food Supplement Program in Delaware, loads monthly food money onto an EBT card you use like a debit card at most grocery stores. Apply online through Delaware ASSIST at assist.dhss.delaware.gov, which handles SNAP, Medicaid, cash assistance, energy help, and WIC on one application, or at any State Service Center. For help, call the Division of Social Services at 302-255-9040.
pine-tree-legal-assistance: Pine Tree Legal Assistance gives free civil legal help to low-income Maine residents on housing and eviction, public benefits like SNAP, TANF, and MaineCare, consumer and debt problems, and more. Call the statewide line at 207-942-8322 during call-in hours: Mondays 12pm to 2:30pm, Tuesdays and Thursdays 9am to 11:30am. Interpreters are free. Free legal information is at ptla.org.
ri-child-care-assistance-program-ccap: The Child Care Assistance Program helps low- and moderate-income Rhode Island families pay for child care so parents can work or train for work. It covers children under 13, or up to 18 with special needs, at licensed and approved providers. Apply online through the HealthyRhode portal at healthyrhode.ri.gov or by phone through the DHS Call Center at 1-855-697-4347.
social-security-ssi-ssdi: SSI provides monthly payments to people 65+ or with disabilities who have very limited income. SSDI covers workers who become disabled.
idaho-careline-2-1-1: Dial 2-1-1 or call 1-800-926-2588 for free, confidential help finding local Idaho assistance with food, housing, utilities, health care, and more. The Idaho CareLine is run by the Department of Health and Welfare and connects you to programs and community resources near you.
unemployment-insurance-mississippi-mdes: Temporary weekly payments if you lost work through no fault of your own, from the Mississippi Department of Employment Security. File online through the ReEmployMS portal at reemployms.mdes.ms.gov, which is fastest, or call the Claimants Line at 601-493-9427, Monday through Friday, 8am to 5pm.
south-carolina-earned-income-tax-credit: South Carolina has a state Earned Income Tax Credit worth 125 percent of your federal EITC, fully phased in since the 2023 tax year. It is nonrefundable, so it lowers the state income tax you owe but does not pay out as a refund beyond that. Claim it with form TC-60 on your South Carolina return. You generally must qualify for the federal EITC first.
west-virginia-snap-food-assistance: SNAP is West Virginia's food assistance program: monthly food money on an EBT card you use like a debit card at most grocery stores. Apply online through wvPATH at wvpath.wv.gov, the state's one application for SNAP, WV WORKS, and Medicaid, at your local Department of Human Services field office, or by phone through the DoHS Customer Service Center at 1-877-716-1212.
virginia-wic: WIC gives healthy food, breastfeeding support, nutrition education, and health referrals to pregnant and postpartum people, infants, and children up to age 5. Virginia WIC runs through local health districts of the Virginia Department of Health. Apply online at myvawic.org, or call 1-877-835-5942 for more information about WIC.
alabama-family-assistance-tanf-cash-assi: Family Assistance is Alabama's TANF cash assistance for low-income families with a child under age 18, or 19 if the child is a full-time student. Most parents take part in the JOBS Program, which helps you find and keep a job. Apply online through OneAlabama at one.alabama.gov or at your county Department of Human Resources office. Cash comes on an EBT card.
rhode-island-snap-food-assistance: SNAP is Rhode Island's food assistance program: monthly food money on an EBT card you use like a debit card at most grocery stores. Apply online through the HealthyRhode portal at healthyrhode.ri.gov, the state's one-stop site that also handles Medicaid, RI Works cash, child care, and energy assistance. You can also apply by phone through the DHS Call Center at 1-855-697-4347 (1-855-MY-RIDHS) or by mail to the RI Department of Human Services.
illinois-earned-income-credit: Illinois' state Earned Income Credit is a refundable tax credit worth 20 percent of your federal Earned Income Tax Credit. If you qualify for the federal EITC, you qualify for the Illinois credit. Claim it on your Illinois state return; free tax-prep sites can file it.
unemployment-insurance-arizona: Temporary weekly payments if you lost work through no fault of your own, from the Arizona Department of Economic Security. You file online, since DES has no walk-in unemployment offices, then file a weekly claim for each week you want to be paid. The UI Call Center is 1-877-600-2722, Monday through Friday, 8am to 5pm Mountain Standard Time.
211-oklahoma: Dial 2-1-1 from any Oklahoma phone for free, confidential help finding local assistance with housing, utility bills, food, healthcare, and more. A resource specialist searches for programs, agencies, and charities near you while you are on the line. You can also find and search your local 2-1-1 online at 211.org.
north-mississippi-rural-legal-services-n: Free civil legal help for low-income residents of the northern 39 counties of Mississippi. North Mississippi Rural Legal Services handles housing, elder law, domestic violence, foreclosure, and other noncriminal matters. Call the intake line at 1-800-898-8731, Monday through Thursday, 9:30am to 3:30pm.
nm-energy-mart-weatherization-program: NM Energy$mart makes free energy-saving retrofits and home modifications for income-eligible New Mexico households, work that lowers future bills. Housing New Mexico (the Mortgage Finance Authority) runs it, and both homeowners and renters can qualify. There is no statewide intake line; you apply through one of three regional service providers assigned to the area where you live, listed on the Housing New Mexico site.
minnesota-family-investment-program-mfip: MFIP is Minnesota's cash and food assistance for low-income families with children, and it is the state's version of TANF. It combines a monthly cash grant with food help and pairs most parents with MFIP Employment Services to move toward work. Apply online at mnbenefits.mn.gov or with a paper Combined Application Form (DHS-5223) at your county or Tribal human services office.
maryland-temporary-cash-assistance-tca: Temporary Cash Assistance, TCA, is Maryland's monthly cash assistance for low-income families with children, and it is the state's version of the federal TANF program. Most adults take part in work activities while they receive it. Apply online through MarylandBenefits at MarylandBenefits.gov or at your local department of social services, or call 1-800-332-6347.
maryland-temporary-disability-assistance: TDAP is Maryland's monthly cash assistance for low-income adults with a disability who do not have dependent children. A licensed medical practitioner must verify the disability. Apply online through MarylandBenefits at MarylandBenefits.gov or at your local department of social services, or call 1-800-332-6347.
north-dakota-211-firstlink: Dial 2-1-1 from any North Dakota phone, or text your ZIP code to 898211, for free, confidential help finding local assistance with housing, utilities, food, and more. FirstLink runs 211 statewide and answers around the clock, every day. FirstLink's office line is 701-293-6462, and it also answers the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline locally.
lifeline-phone-and-internet-discount: Monthly discount on phone or internet service for low-income households.
indiana-211: Dial 2-1-1 from any Indiana phone, or call 1-866-211-9966, for free, confidential help finding local assistance with housing, utilities, food, healthcare, and more. Indiana 211 is a statewide service with trained navigators answering around the clock, every day. You can also text your zip code to 898-211 or search at in211.org.
alaska-2-1-1: Dial 2-1-1 from any Alaska phone for free, confidential help finding local assistance with housing, utilities, food, health care, and more. Alaska 2-1-1 is a statewide service of United Way of Anchorage that refers you to the programs and funds near you. You can also search at alaska211.org.
capk-energy-program-help-with-utility-bi: CAPK (Community Action Partnership of Kern) helps income-qualified households pay electric, gas, and propane bills, and can weatherize your home to lower future bills. Apply by email, mail, or in person at 300 19th Street in Bakersfield.
unemployment-insurance-delaware: Temporary weekly payments if you lost work through no fault of your own, from the Delaware Department of Labor, Division of Unemployment Insurance. File your claim online through the Division's claim system, linked from labor.delaware.gov, which is the fastest way. For help, call the statewide Unemployment Insurance line at 302-761-8446.
maine-wic-nutrition-program: WIC gives healthy food, nutrition education, breastfeeding and lactation support, and health referrals to pregnant and postpartum people, infants, and children up to age 5. Maine WIC runs through local agencies across the state and is open to anyone living in Maine, including migrant workers. Contact your local WIC office to apply, or call 1-800-437-9300 for more information.
home-weatherization-assistance-program-i: Free home energy-efficiency work for income-eligible Illinoisans: air sealing, insulation, and heating-system repairs that lower future bills. Run through Community Action Agencies and overseen by the Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity. The Help Illinois Families call center is 1-833-711-0374.
weatherization-assistance-program-new-ha: Free home energy-efficiency work for income-eligible New Hampshire households: insulation, air sealing, and heating-system improvements that lower future bills. The New Hampshire Department of Energy runs it through the state's Community Action Agencies, and both homeowners and renters can qualify. Contact the Community Action Agency serving your area to apply, since the state does not take applications directly.
idaho-energy-assistance-liheap-heating-a: LIHEAP helps low-income Idaho households pay winter heating bills, with a Crisis part that works year-round to stop a shutoff or restore disconnected service. The program runs through Community Action Partnership agencies that serve every Idaho county. Find your local agency by dialing 2-1-1, and watch the seasonal application dates.
medicaid-illinois-hfs: Illinois Medicaid is free or low-cost health coverage run by the Department of Healthcare and Family Services. Adults 19 to 64 can qualify with income up to 138 percent of the federal poverty level under the ACA Adult category. Apply online at ABE (abe.illinois.gov), by phone at the DHS Help Line 1-800-843-6154, or at a Family Community Resource Center.
alaska-child-care-assistance-program: The Child Care Assistance Program helps low-income working families in Alaska pay for child care, funded through the federal Child Care Development Fund. It lowers what you pay a licensed or approved provider so you can work, look for work, or go to school. Call the Child Care Program Office at 907-269-4500 or toll-free 888-268-4632 to start.
idaho-child-care-program-iccp: The Idaho Child Care Program helps eligible parents pay part of their child care costs while they work, go to school, or attend job training. It covers children under 13, or older children who have a disability. Apply online at idalink.idaho.gov or by phone at 1-877-456-1233.
minnesota-child-tax-credit: Minnesota's Child Tax Credit is a refundable credit of $1,750 for each qualifying child under age 18, with no limit on the number of children. Because it is refundable, it can come back to you as cash even if you owe no tax. The credit begins to phase out once income passes $31,950, or $37,910 for a married couple filing jointly. Claim it on Schedule M1CWFC with your Minnesota return.
all-kids-illinois-childrens-health-cover: All Kids is Illinois' health coverage for children, covering doctor visits, dental, vision, and more. Many families pay no premiums or co-payments. Apply online, on paper, or with help from a partner; the All Kids Hotline is 1-866-255-5437.
hawaii-snap-food-assistance: SNAP is Hawaii's food assistance program, run by the Department of Human Services (DHS): monthly food money loaded onto an EBT card you use like a debit card at most grocery stores. The fastest way to apply is online through the DHS Public Assistance Information System (PAIS) at pais.dhs.hawaii.gov, which handles SNAP and financial assistance on one application. You can also mail or drop off a paper form at a processing center, or call the Public Assistance Information Line at 1-855-643-1643, open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
united-way-211-missouri: Dial 2-1-1 from any Missouri phone, or call 1-800-427-4626, for free, confidential help finding local assistance with housing, utilities, food, healthcare, and more. United Way 211 answers around the clock, every day of the year, with multilingual specialists. You can also search the statewide resource directory at 211helps.org.
unemployment-insurance-tennessee: Temporary weekly payments if you lost work through no fault of your own, from the Tennessee Department of Labor and Workforce Development. File online at Jobs4TN.gov, which is the fastest way, or call the Employment Security line at 1-844-224-5818.
hawaii-tanf-cash-assistance: Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) is Hawaii's monthly cash assistance for low-income families that include a minor child and a caretaker relative. Families with mixed or non-citizen immigration status may instead qualify for the state-funded Temporary Assistance for Other Needy Families (TAONF), which provides the same benefits. Apply online through the DHS Public Assistance Information System at pais.dhs.hawaii.gov or by paper form. As a condition of eligibility, most families take part in the First-To-Work program.
weatherization-assistance-program-tdhca: Free home energy improvements for low-income Texans: insulation, caulking, duct work, and repair or replacement of inefficient heating and cooling systems, so future bills shrink. Apply through the weatherization agency that serves your county.
south-carolina-snap-food-assistance: SNAP is South Carolina's food assistance program: monthly food money on an EBT card you use like a debit card at most grocery stores. The Department of Social Services runs it. Apply online through the DSS Benefits Portal at benefitsportal.dss.sc.gov, in person at your county DSS office, or by mail or fax. To check a case or request a form, call the DSS Connect Call Center at 1-800-616-1309.
211-colorado: Dial 2-1-1 from any Colorado phone, or call 1-866-760-6489, for free, confidential help finding local assistance with housing, utilities, food, healthcare, and more. 211 Colorado covers all 64 counties and updates its resource database daily. You can also text your zip code to 898-211 or search at 211colorado.org.
snap-food-benefits-lone-star-card: Texas SNAP puts monthly grocery money on a Lone Star Card that works like a debit card at any store that accepts SNAP. Apply online at YourTexasBenefits.com or call 2-1-1 for help.
211-maine: Dial 2-1-1 from any Maine phone, or call 1-866-811-5695, for free, confidential help finding local assistance with housing, utilities, food, healthcare, and more. 211 Maine answers around the clock, every day, in all languages. You can also text your zip code to 898-211, or call 1-877-463-6207 from out of state.
wisconsin-home-energy-assistance-program: WHEAP is Wisconsin's LIHEAP program: help with heating and electric costs, plus emergency (crisis) assistance and furnace repair or replacement for income-eligible households. Apply online at energybenefit.wi.gov, or contact the local energy assistance agency serving your county or tribe. For more information, call 1-866-432-8947. The main heating benefit runs October 1 through May 15 each year.
city-of-king-utility-billing-and-collect: The City of King bills you for city water and sewer. If you cannot pay your bill on time, call the billing office before the due date. Unpaid bills can get late fees and your service can be shut off. You can pay in person at 229 S. Main Street, online, or by phone at 1-844-778-1892.
nfcc-nonprofit-credit-counseling: Free or low-cost counseling from nonprofit agencies: budgeting, debt management plans, and negotiating with creditors. A safe alternative to for-profit "debt relief" companies.
utah-legal-services-and-timpanogos-legal: Utah Legal Services provides free civil legal help to low-income Utahns on housing and eviction, family, public benefits, consumer, and other noncriminal matters. Call 801-328-8891 or apply online at utahlegalservices.org. In Utah County, Timpanogos Legal Center runs a free legal advice hotline for self-represented people at 801-649-8895, Monday through Friday, 9am to 2pm.
delaware-wic: WIC gives healthy food, breastfeeding support, nutrition education, and health referrals to pregnant and postpartum people, infants, and children up to age 5. Delaware WIC runs through the Division of Public Health. Start your application through Delaware ASSIST at assist.dhss.delaware.gov, then call your county WIC office to set up an appointment. In New Castle County, call 302-605-4066.
idaho-snap-food-stamps: SNAP, still called food stamps, puts monthly food money on an Idaho EBT card you use like a debit card at grocery stores. Apply online at idalink.idaho.gov, the state benefits portal that also handles Medicaid, cash assistance, and child care help, or by phone at 1-877-456-1233. As of February 15, 2026, candy and soda are no longer SNAP-eligible purchases in Idaho.
connecticut-snap-food-assistance: SNAP is Connecticut's food assistance program: monthly food money on an EBT card you use like a debit card at most grocery stores. Apply online through ConneCT at connect.ct.gov or the MyDSS mobile portal, by mail, or in person at a DSS office. You can also call the DSS Benefits Center at 1-855-626-6632, Monday through Friday, 8am to 4pm.
legal-action-of-wisconsin-free-civil-leg: Legal Action of Wisconsin provides free civil legal help to low-income residents on housing, family, public benefits, consumer, and other noncriminal matters. As of January 1, 2026 it merged with Wisconsin Judicare into a single statewide firm that also serves northern Wisconsin and tribal communities. Call the intake line at 1-855-947-2529, weekdays 9am to 4pm, or apply online any time at legalaction.org.
unemployment-insurance-minnesota: Temporary weekly payments if you lost work through no fault of your own, from Minnesota's Unemployment Insurance program at DEED. Apply online at uimn.org, which is the fastest way, or by phone at 1-877-898-9090 for Greater Minnesota or 651-296-3644 in the Twin Cities, Monday through Friday, 8am to 4:30pm. Phone service is offered in English, Spanish, Hmong, and Somali.
kentucky-wic: WIC gives healthy food, breastfeeding support, nutrition education, and health referrals to pregnant, breastfeeding, and postpartum women, infants, and children up to age 5. Kentucky WIC runs through local health departments. Call the state WIC line at 1-877-597-0367 to find your local clinic, or learn more at the Cabinet for Health and Family Services WIC page.
michigan-earned-income-tax-credit: Michigan's Earned Income Tax Credit for Working Families is worth 30 percent of your federal EITC and is refundable, so it can put money in your pocket even if you owe no state tax. Public Act 4 of 2023 raised it from 6 percent to 30 percent. Claim it by filing a Michigan MI-1040 return after you qualify for the federal EITC.
calfresh-food-stamps-kern-county-dhs: Monthly money on an EBT card to buy groceries. If you have very little income or cash on hand, you may qualify for expedited benefits within 3 days.
liheap-home-energy-assistance-2: Pennsylvania's LIHEAP helps low-income households pay heating bills with a cash grant, plus a separate Crisis grant when heat is shut off, about to be, or broken. Apply at COMPASS during the season; the LIHEAP Helpline is 1-866-857-7095.
211-new-hampshire: Dial 2-1-1 from any New Hampshire phone, or call 1-866-444-4211, for free, confidential help finding local assistance with housing, utilities, food, health care, and more. 211 NH is answered by trained specialists 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. You can also reach them by text or email through 211nh.org.
child-health-plus: New York's health coverage for children under 19 who don't qualify for Medicaid, with no income cap to enroll. Coverage is free for families under about 2.2 times the poverty level; higher-income families pay $15 to $60 per child per month. Apply through NY State of Health or call 1-800-698-4543.
texaslawhelp-org-eviction-and-legal-help: Free legal information, forms, and guides for Texans, run by the nonprofit Texas Legal Services Center. The eviction section explains the notices, deadlines, and court steps, and connects you with legal aid.
988-suicide-and-crisis-lifeline: Free, confidential support 24/7 for anyone in emotional distress or crisis. Call or text 988.
new-hampshire-fanf-tanf-cash-assistance: Financial Assistance to Needy Families, FANF, is New Hampshire's monthly cash assistance for low-income families with dependent children, also known as TANF. Most adults take part in the New Hampshire Employment Program, NHEP, which helps you move toward a job. Apply online through NH EASY at nheasy.nh.gov or at your local DHHS District Office.
new-mexico-works-tanf-cash-assistance: New Mexico Works, the state's TANF program, is a monthly cash benefit for low-income families with children, loaded onto an EBT card you can use like a debit card. It helps cover basics like housing, utilities, and clothing while adults work toward a job. Apply online through YESNM at yes.nm.gov or at your local Income Support Division office. Questions go to 1-800-283-4465.
mainecare-maine-medicaid: MaineCare is Maine's Medicaid program, free or low-cost health insurance for children, pregnant people, parents, older adults, people with disabilities, and low-income adults. Maine expanded MaineCare, so low-income adults now qualify on income alone. Apply online through My Maine Connection at mymaineconnection.gov, or call the Office for Family Independence at 1-855-797-4357.
oregon-tanf-cash-assistance: Temporary Assistance for Needy Families, TANF, is Oregon's monthly cash assistance for low-income families with children, pregnant people, and young heads of household. A family of three with no other income can get up to $506 a month. Apply online through ONE at one.oregon.gov, at a local Oregon Department of Human Services office, or by phone at 800-699-9075. Most adults take part in the JOBS employment program.
weatherization-assistance-oregon: Free home energy-efficiency work for income-eligible Oregon households: insulation, air sealing, and heating-system improvements that lower future bills, including a Home Oil Weatherization option for oil-heated homes. Oregon Housing and Community Services runs the program through local Community Action Agencies. Contact the agency serving your county, or reach Oregon Housing and Community Services at 800-453-5511, to apply.
crisis-fuel-assistance-vermont: Crisis Fuel Assistance helps when you have a winter heating emergency, like running out of fuel with no money to buy more. It can buy your primary heating source, pay for electricity needed to run your heating system, and help set up payment plans or prevent a gas or electric disconnection. Apply in person at your local Community Action Agency, and call first so they can tell you what to bring. Do not wait until you run out, because the program cannot help once fuel is already delivered or furnace work is done.
temporary-cash-assistance-tca: Monthly cash for very-low-income Florida families with children under 18, plus pregnant women in some circumstances. The Relative Caregiver Program pays monthly amounts to relatives raising a court-ordered dependent child. Apply through MyACCESS.
tanf-cash-assistance-illinois: Illinois TANF pays monthly cash to pregnant people and families with children, loaded on the Illinois Link card. Adults are limited to 60 months of cash assistance in a lifetime. Apply online at ABE (abe.illinois.gov) or at your local Family Community Resource Center; the DHS Help Line is 1-800-843-6154.
vermont-legal-aid-and-legal-services-ver: Vermont Legal Aid and Legal Services Vermont work together to give free civil legal help to low-income Vermonters on housing and eviction, family, public benefits, consumer and debt, health care, and other noncriminal problems. Legal Services Vermont screens all requests. The fastest way in is the online Legal Help Request Form, or leave a message on the legal helpline at 1-800-889-2047 (Monday, Wednesday, and Friday 8am to 1pm; Tuesday and Thursday 12:30pm to 7pm). Most people hear back within about 5 to 10 days. Free self-help legal information is at vtlawhelp.org for everyone.
legal-aid-of-wyoming: Legal Aid of Wyoming provides free civil legal help to low-income residents on noncriminal matters like eviction and housing, family law, public benefits, and consumer problems. Call the statewide line at 1-877-432-9955, Monday through Friday, 9am to 4pm, or apply online at lawyoming.org/apply-online. Offices serve the state from Cheyenne, Casper, Lander, and Gillette.
weatherization-assistance-program-washin: Free home energy-efficiency work for income-eligible Washington households: insulation, air sealing, ventilation, and related repairs that lower future bills. The Department of Commerce funds the work through local agencies. Both homeowners and renters can qualify. Contact the weatherization agency serving your county to apply, since Commerce does not take applications directly.
tennessee-community-action-agencies-util: Tennessee's community action agencies help low-income households with utility bills, home energy costs, and other emergencies, and they deliver programs like LIHEAP and weatherization at the local level. There are 19 agencies covering all 95 counties. Find the one serving your county through the Tennessee Association of Community Action at tncommunityaction.org.
south-carolina-family-independence-tanf-: Family Independence, South Carolina's TANF program, gives monthly cash assistance to low-income families with children through the Department of Social Services. Most adults take part in a TANF work program run through SC Works. Apply online through the DSS Benefits Portal at benefitsportal.dss.sc.gov, at your county DSS office, or by mail or fax. Call 1-800-616-1309 for a form or a case question.
utah-medicaid: Utah Medicaid is free or low-cost health coverage for children, pregnant people, parents, older adults, people with disabilities, and low-income adults. Utah expanded Medicaid in 2020 to cover adults with low income, so it is worth applying even if you were turned down before. Apply online through myCase at jobs.utah.gov/mycase, or call the Medicaid information line at 1-866-608-9422.
fuel-assistance-liheap-massachusetts: Fuel Assistance, the Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP), helps income-eligible Massachusetts households pay winter heating bills, whether you heat with oil, gas, electricity, propane, or wood. Local Fuel Assistance agencies take applications; the online season opens October 1. Find your agency or apply through the HEAP portal, and call the Cold Relief Heatline at 1-800-632-8175 with questions.
unemployment-insurance-hawaii: Unemployment Insurance from the Hawaii Department of Labor and Industrial Relations (DLIR) pays weekly benefits if you lost work through no fault of your own. File your claim online through the UI website at labor.hawaii.gov/ui, then file a claim certification for each week. For help, the statewide UI Call Center is 1-833-901-2272 toll-free, or 808-762-5752.
calworks-kern-county-dhs: Monthly cash aid and job help for families with children and pregnant women. Can also help pay for childcare, diapers, transportation, and even housing assistance.
crisis-control-ministry: Crisis Control Ministry helps Stokes and Forsyth County residents in a short-term emergency. They can help pay rent or mortgage, utility bills, and heating fuel. They also run a food pantry where you choose your own food and a free licensed pharmacy. Call to set up a phone or in-person interview.
weatherization-assistance-program-pa-dce: Free home energy-efficiency work for income-eligible Pennsylvanians: insulation, air sealing, and heating-system fixes that lower future bills. Funded by the U.S. Department of Energy and run through Community Action Agencies in every county, overseen by the Department of Community and Economic Development.
tanf-cash-assistance-for-families: Monthly cash assistance and work support for very-low-income families with children. Run by states under different names.
kern-county-aging-and-adult-services-sen: One phone call connects seniors and their families to meals on wheels, in-home care, transportation, utility rebate help, and legal services. Staff can also help you fill out forms and understand letters from other agencies.
ohio-earned-income-credit: Ohio's state Earned Income Credit is worth 30 percent of your federal Earned Income Tax Credit. It is nonrefundable, so it can lower your Ohio income tax to zero but does not pay out beyond that. Claim it on the Ohio Schedule of Credits with your state return.
weatherization-assistance-program-missis: Free home energy-efficiency work for income-eligible Mississippi households: insulation, air sealing, and furnace repair or replacement that lower future bills. Apply through the Access MS portal at access.ms.gov, pick Community Services, and your local Community Action Agency handles the rest. Homeowners and renters both qualify. Call MDHS Community Services at 1-800-421-0762.
illinois-legal-aid-online-eviction-and-l: Free, plain-language legal information for Illinoisans, guided court-form tools, and a directory to find a local legal aid provider. Illinois Legal Aid Online covers eviction, benefits, family law, debt, and more.
weatherization-assistance-alaska-housing: Alaska's Weatherization program makes energy-efficiency repairs at no cost to income-eligible households: air sealing, insulation, and heating-system work that lowers future bills. The Alaska Housing Finance Corporation, AHFC, runs it through regional providers, and both homeowners and renters can qualify, including condos. Contact your regional weatherization provider to apply, or call AHFC at 907-338-6100 or 800-478-2432 in Alaska.
new-mexico-wic: WIC gives healthy food, breastfeeding support, nutrition education, and health referrals to pregnant and postpartum people, infants, and children up to age 5. New Mexico WIC runs through the state Department of Health. Request an appointment or check eligibility at nmwic.org, or call 1-866-867-3124 to learn more and find the clinic nearest you.
unemployment-benefits-washington-esd: Temporary weekly payments if you lost work through no fault of your own, from the Washington Employment Security Department. File online through eServices at esd.wa.gov, which is the fastest way and open around the clock, or call the claims center at 1-800-318-6022. After you apply, you must file a weekly claim for each week to be paid.
unemployment-insurance-massachusetts-dua: Temporary weekly payments if you lost work through no fault of your own, from the Department of Unemployment Assistance (DUA). File online through UI Online at mass.gov/dua, available daily from 6am to 10pm, or by phone through the TeleClaim Center at 1-877-626-6800, Monday through Thursday, 8:30am to 4:30pm. The phone line is closed Fridays so staff can process claims.
pipp-plus-percentage-of-income-payment-p: PIPP Plus lets income-eligible Ohioans on a PUCO-regulated utility pay a set percentage of household income toward gas and electric bills instead of the full amount, with a $10 monthly minimum. As of April 2026 it is run by the Ohio Department of Job and Family Services. Apply online, by appointment, or by mail through your local Energy Assistance Provider.
dc-earned-income-tax-credit: The District's Earned Income Tax Credit is one of the most generous in the country. For Tax Year 2025, the DC EITC equals 100 percent of your federal EITC, and it is refundable, so you may receive a refund even if you owe no DC income tax. Claim it on your DC individual income tax return, the D-40. Questions go to the Office of Tax and Revenue at (202) 727-4829, which spells (202) 727-4TAX.
oklahoma-child-care-subsidy: The Oklahoma Child Care Subsidy helps eligible families pay for child care while parents work, train, or go to school. Apply online at OKDHSLive.org, at your local Oklahoma Human Services office, or by phone at 405-522-5050. Families may owe a copay based on income, family size, and how many children need care.
arhome-arkansas-medicaid-expansion: ARHOME, Arkansas Health and Opportunity for Me, is Arkansas's expanded Medicaid for low-income adults ages 19 to 64. It uses Medicaid dollars to enroll most members in a private qualified health plan that covers doctor visits, prescriptions, and hospital care. Apply online through Access Arkansas at access.arkansas.gov, or call 1-855-372-1084.
med-quest-hawaii-medicaid: Med-QUEST is Hawaii's Medicaid program: free or low-cost health coverage for children, pregnant women, parents, seniors, people with disabilities, and low-income adults. Hawaii expanded Medicaid, so low-income adults without children can qualify too. Apply online at the Med-QUEST Online Portal, medical.mybenefits.hawaii.gov, or call Med-QUEST Customer Service at 1-800-316-8005.
catholic-charities-bakersfield-community: Emergency help with rent or mortgage payments, plus a food pantry and clothing for families in crisis. You do not need to be Catholic to get help.
golden-empire-gleaners: A Bakersfield food bank working with over 125 community agencies to get groceries to Kern County families in need. Call or stop by the warehouse on 30th Street to get connected to food help.
unemployment-insurance-oregon: Temporary weekly payments if you lost work through no fault of your own, from the Oregon Employment Department. File online through Frances Online at frances.oregon.gov, which is available 24 hours a day and is the easiest way, or apply by phone at 1-877-345-3484 (1-877-File-4-UI). You then file a claim for each week to keep payments coming.
michigan-211: Dial 2-1-1 from any Michigan phone, or call 844-875-9211, for free, confidential help finding local assistance with housing, utilities, food, healthcare, and more. Michigan 211 runs through seven regional call centers, covers the whole state, and answers around the clock. You can also text your zip code to 898211 or search at mi211.org.
211-warmline-district-of-columbia: Dial 2-1-1 from any District phone, or call (202) 463-6211 from out of state, to reach the 211 Warmline, the District's centralized hub for social service resources and referrals. Staff help you find local assistance with housing, utilities, food, healthcare, and more. The Warmline answers Monday through Friday, 9am to 5pm; after hours, leave a detailed voicemail and a call agent returns your call within 1 to 2 business days.
alaska-senior-benefits-program: The Alaska Senior Benefits Program pays a monthly cash benefit of $125, $175, or $250 to low-income Alaskans age 65 and older, with the amount set by your other income. Savings and resources do not count. Apply online through the Alaska Connect portal or by phone at 800-478-7778, and the benefit arrives by direct deposit or an Alaska Quest EBT card.
nevada-energy-assistance-program-liheap: Nevada's Energy Assistance Program, the state's LIHEAP, helps low-income households pay heating and cooling bills. It runs year-round rather than in seasonal windows, but once you get a benefit you generally cannot reapply until about 11 months later. Apply online through Access Nevada at accessnevada.nv.gov, or submit a paper application by mail, fax, email, or at a welfare office drop box. Call 775-684-0800 with questions.
lawhelp-org-free-legal-aid: Find free legal aid in your state for evictions, debt collection, benefits denials, and family issues.
nebraska-child-care-subsidy: The Child Care Subsidy helps low-income families pay for child care while parents work, go to school, or train for a job. Apply online through iServe Nebraska at iserve.nebraska.gov. For questions about your eligibility, call the Child Care Subsidy Program at 402-471-9152.
oregon-energy-assistance-liheap-oeap: Oregon Housing and Community Services helps income-eligible households with home heating and cooling bills through the federal LIHEAP program and the Oregon Energy Assistance Program. You do not apply to the state directly; you apply through the local Community Action Agency serving your county. Find your agency through Oregon Housing and Community Services at 800-453-5511 or by dialing 2-1-1.
alabama-wic: WIC gives healthy food, breastfeeding support, nutrition education, and health referrals to pregnant and postpartum women, infants, and children under age 5. Alabama WIC runs through county health departments of the Alabama Department of Public Health. Contact your county health department for an appointment, or call the statewide WIC line at 1-888-942-4673.
feeding-america-food-bank-locator: Find your nearest food bank and free food distribution. No paperwork needed at most pantries.
unemployment-insurance-louisiana: Temporary weekly payments if you lost work through no fault of your own, from the Louisiana Workforce Commission. File online through the HiRE self-service system at louisianaworks.net, which is the fastest way, or call the UI Call Center at 1-866-783-5567, Monday through Friday, 8am to 4:30pm.
weatherization-assistance-program-idaho: Free home energy-efficiency work for income-eligible Idaho households: insulation, air sealing, and heating-system repair or replacement that lower future bills. Community Action Partnership agencies run the program locally, so contact the agency serving your area to apply. Renters can qualify with written landlord permission.
arizona-wic: WIC gives healthy food, breastfeeding support, nutrition education, and health referrals to pregnant and postpartum people, infants, and children up to age 5. The Arizona Department of Health Services runs it through local clinics. Call 1-800-252-5942 to find the clinic nearest you, or start online at azdhs.gov.
oregon-earned-income-credit: The Oregon Earned Income Credit is a refundable state credit for working people who qualify for the federal Earned Income Tax Credit. It is worth 9 percent of your federal EITC, and 12 percent if you have a dependent who is younger than 3 at the end of the tax year. Because it is refundable, it can come back to you as a refund even if you owe no Oregon tax. Claim it on your Oregon return.
ohio-works-first-cash-assistance: Ohio Works First is the cash-assistance part of Ohio's TANF program, paying monthly cash on the Way2Go debit card to low-income families with children. Ohio sets a 36-month state time limit on benefits. Apply online through Ohio Benefits at benefits.ohio.gov or at your County Department of Job and Family Services.
work-first-family-assistance-north-carol: Work First is North Carolina's TANF program, giving short-term cash assistance and work services to low-income families with children. Cash is provided primarily for the children, and the program pairs it with help finding a job. Apply online at epass.nc.gov or at your county Department of Social Services.
unemployment-insurance-kansas: Temporary weekly payments if you lost work through no fault of your own, from the Kansas Department of Labor.
