File your claim and your weekly certifications through the Claimant Self Service Portal linked at dol.ks.gov/unemployment. If you need help, the Contact Center is 1-800-292-6333 (local 785-575-1460), open during weekday business hours (Thursday closes earlier).
unemployment-insurance-job-service-north: Temporary weekly payments if you lost work through no fault of your own, from Job Service North Dakota. File online through the UI ICE claims system at apps.nd.gov, which is the fastest way, or get help from the Unemployment Insurance Customer Service line at 701-328-1680.
alabama-community-action-agencies: Community Action Agencies are the local nonprofits that pull together help for low-income Alabama families in one place: utility and energy assistance including LIHEAP, weatherization, and often emergency aid, food, and job support. Find the agency serving your county through the Community Action Association of Alabama's agency locator, or dial 2-1-1.
unemployment-insurance-south-carolina-de: Temporary weekly payments if you lost work through no fault of your own, from the South Carolina Department of Employment and Workforce. File your claim online through the MyBenefits portal at dew.sc.gov, which is the fastest way. For help, call 1-866-831-1724, or use Relay 711. You must file a weekly claim to keep payments coming.
legal-aid-of-arkansas: Legal Aid of Arkansas is a nonprofit law firm that gives free civil legal help to low-income Arkansans on eviction and housing, family and domestic abuse, consumer and debt, disability, and public benefits problems. As of 2026 it serves the whole state as the sole federally funded legal aid program. Call the free HELP Line at 1-800-952-9243, or apply online at arlegalaid.org.
texas-medicaid-and-chip: Free or low-cost health coverage for low-income Texas children, pregnant women, seniors, and people with disabilities. CHIP covers children in families that earn too much for Medicaid; one application at YourTexasBenefits.com checks both.
211-community-resource-helpline: Free, confidential helpline that connects you with local assistance programs of every kind — rent, utilities, food, shelter, healthcare, and more. Available 24/7 in most areas, in many languages.
legal-services-of-new-jersey-lsnj-law-ho: Legal Services of New Jersey gives free civil legal help to low-income residents on housing, family, public benefits, consumer, employment, and immigration matters. Call the statewide LSNJ-LAW hotline at 1-888-576-5529, open Monday through Friday, 8am to 5:30pm, or find free legal information and self-help tools at lsnjlaw.org.
nevada-wic: WIC gives healthy food, breastfeeding support, nutrition education, and health referrals to pregnant and postpartum people, infants, and children up to age 5. Nevada WIC runs clinics in urban and rural communities statewide. Find your nearest clinic and apply at nevadawic.org, or call 1-800-863-8942 for help getting started.
alabama-medicaid: Alabama Medicaid is free or low-cost health coverage for children, pregnant women, parents with very low income, older adults, and people with disabilities. Alabama has not expanded Medicaid, so adults without dependent children generally do not qualify no matter how low their income. Call the Medicaid Recipient Call Center at 1-800-362-1504, Monday through Friday, 8am to 4:30pm, to ask questions or find the district office that takes applications.
wyoming-211: Dial 2-1-1 from any Wyoming phone for free, confidential help finding local assistance with housing, utilities, food, healthcare, and more. Wyoming 211 is a statewide referral service; give a short version of what you need and where you live, and a specialist searches for programs near you. You can also search at wyoming211.org.
new-jersey-wic: WIC gives healthy food, breastfeeding support, nutrition education, and health referrals to pregnant and postpartum women, infants, and children up to age 5. New Jersey WIC is offered through local agencies statewide. Start a pre-screening at wic.nj.gov, then a local agency follows up to schedule your first appointment.
green-mountain-care-vermont-medicaid-and: Green Mountain Care is the umbrella name for Vermont's public health coverage, including Medicaid and Dr. Dynasaur, which covers children under 19 and pregnant people. Vermont expanded Medicaid, so low-income adults under 65 can qualify too, alongside people 65 or older, blind, or disabled. Apply for Medicaid, Dr. Dynasaur, and other coverage through Vermont Health Connect online or by calling 1-855-899-9600, Monday through Friday, 8am to 4:30pm. Current members can reach the Customer Support Center at 1-800-250-8427.
211-connecticut: Dial 2-1-1 from any Connecticut phone, or call 1-800-203-1234, for free, confidential help finding local assistance with housing, utilities, food, healthcare, and more. 211 Connecticut is a program of United Way of Connecticut and answers around the clock, every day. You can also chat or search at 211ct.org.
unemployment-insurance-new-mexico: Temporary weekly payments if you lost work through no fault of your own, from the New Mexico Department of Workforce Solutions. File online through the state's workforce portal at jobs.dws.nm.gov, which is the fastest way, then file a weekly certification for each week you want to be paid. You must be able to work, available for work, and looking for work while you claim.
weatherization-assistance-program-maryla: Free home energy-efficiency work for income-eligible Maryland households: insulation, air sealing, and heating-system improvements that lower future bills. The Department of Housing and Community Development runs the program through local weatherization agencies. Contact the local agency serving your area to apply, or call 1-855-583-8976 for help finding it.
alaska-wic: WIC gives free healthy foods, breastfeeding support, nutrition education, and health referrals to pregnant and postpartum people, infants, and children under age 5. Alaska WIC runs through local clinics across the state. Call the state WIC office at 907-465-3100 to find your local clinic and start, or look up a clinic by region online.
nebraska-211-united-way-of-the-midlands: Dial 2-1-1 from any Nebraska phone, or call 1-866-813-1731, for free, confidential help finding local assistance with housing, utilities, food, and more. Nebraska 211 is run by United Way of the Midlands. You can also text your zip code to 898211, or chat and search at ne211.org, with live chat open 7am to 10pm every day.
missouri-temporary-assistance-cash-assis: Temporary Assistance, TA, is Missouri's monthly cash benefit for low-income families with children, meant to help cover costs like clothing and utilities. Most adults take part in the Missouri Work Assistance program, which helps you move toward a job. Apply online at mydss.mo.gov or ask for a paper application through the FSD Information Center at 1-855-373-4636.
reemployment-assistance-unemployment: Florida's unemployment benefits: temporary, partial income replacement if you lost work through no fault of your own. FloridaCommerce runs the program; apply online through the Reconnect system at FloridaJobs.org.
unemployment-insurance-missouri: Temporary weekly payments if you lost work through no fault of your own, from the Missouri Division of Employment Security. File online through UInteract at uinteract.labor.mo.gov, which is the fastest way and open 24 hours a day, or call a Regional Claims Center at 1-800-320-2519, Monday through Friday, 8am to 5pm Central.
health-insurance-marketplace-healthcare-: Subsidized health insurance if you don't qualify for Medicaid. Losing a job or income counts as a special enrollment event.
illinois-wic: Healthy food on a WIC EBT card, nutrition education, and breastfeeding support for pregnant and new mothers, infants, and children under 5. Find your local office through the DHS Office Locator and make an appointment; the State WIC Office is 1-844-901-0962.
maryland-legal-aid: Maryland Legal Aid provides free civil legal help to low-income residents on housing and eviction, public benefits, family, consumer, and other noncriminal matters. Call the statewide intake line at 1-888-465-2468 to reach the office serving your area, or start an application online and find your local office at marylandlegalaid.org.
weatherization-assistance-program-vermon: Vermont's Weatherization Assistance Program makes free energy-efficiency improvements so your home wastes less heat and your bills drop. On average the program makes about 10,000 dollars of improvements per home, adds around 1,500 square feet of insulation, and cuts drafts by about 40 percent. There is no statewide phone line; you apply through the Community Action Agency serving your area, which are BROC, Capstone, CVOEO, NETO, and SEVCA. Download your agency's application, complete it, and mail the signed forms to the address on the application.
211-virginia: Dial 2-1-1 from any Virginia phone, or call 1-800-230-6977, for free, confidential help finding local assistance with housing, utilities, food, healthcare, and more. 211 Virginia is a statewide service that answers around the clock, every day. You can also text the keyword CONNECT to 247211 or search at 211virginia.org.
legal-aid-of-north-carolina: Legal Aid of North Carolina is the statewide nonprofit law firm that gives free civil legal help to people with low incomes, covering eviction, unsafe housing, domestic violence, public benefits, and more. Apply by phone at 1-866-219-5262 or online through the JusticeHub portal at legalaidnc.org/apply.
healthy-connections-medicaid-south-carol: Healthy Connections is South Carolina Medicaid: free or low-cost health coverage run by the Department of Health and Human Services for children, pregnant people, low-income parents, older adults, and people with disabilities. South Carolina has not expanded Medicaid, so most adults without children do not qualify on low income alone. Apply online at apply.scdhhs.gov, or call the Member Contact Center at 1-888-549-0820, Monday through Friday, 8am to 6pm.
north-dakota-child-care-assistance-progr: The Child Care Assistance Program, CCAP, helps eligible low-income North Dakota families pay for child care while parents work, look for work, or attend school or training. Apply online through the Self Service Portal at applyforhelp.nd.gov, which also covers SNAP, Medicaid, LIHEAP, and TANF, or by phone through the HHS Customer Support Center at 1-866-614-6005.
dc-tanf-cash-assistance: Temporary Assistance for Needy Families, TANF, is the District's monthly cash assistance for low-income families with children. Most adults take part in the TANF Employment and Education Program, TEP, which coaches you toward work and education goals. Apply online at districtdirect.dc.gov or by phone through the Public Benefits Call Center at (202) 727-5355. Effective October 2025, the maximum monthly benefit runs from $504 for a household of one up to larger amounts for bigger families.
california-courts-self-help-eviction: Official guides on responding to an eviction notice in California — you typically have only 5 business days to respond to a court summons. Free self-help centers at every courthouse.
rhode-island-energy-assistance-liheap: The Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program, LIHEAP, helps income-eligible Rhode Island households with home heating and energy costs, and it runs through the RI Department of Human Services. Apply online through the HealthyRhode portal at healthyrhode.ri.gov, by mail, or by phone through the DHS Call Center at 1-855-697-4347. Weatherization is a separate program that fixes the home itself.
dc-snap-food-assistance: SNAP is the District's food assistance program: monthly food money on an EBT card you use like a debit card at most grocery stores. Apply online at districtdirect.dc.gov, by phone through the Department of Human Services Public Benefits Call Center at (202) 727-5355, or in person at an Economic Security Administration service center. The District also adds a local Temporary Local Benefit, Give SNAP a Raise, of up to 10 percent of a household's federal maximum benefit.
massachusetts-wic-nutrition-program: WIC gives healthy food, breastfeeding support, nutrition education, and health referrals to pregnant and postpartum people, infants, and children up to age 5. Massachusetts WIC runs through local clinics. Begin online at mass.gov, or call 1-800-942-1007, Monday through Friday, 9am to 5pm, to reach the WIC clinic nearest you and set up an appointment.
weatherization-assistance-program-kentuc: Kentucky's Weatherization Assistance Program makes free energy-efficiency repairs for income-eligible households: insulation, air sealing, and heating-system fixes that lower future bills. Kentucky Housing Corporation runs the program and it is delivered by local Community Action Agencies, so you apply through the agency serving your county. Homeowners and renters can both qualify.
nc-211: Dial 2-1-1 from any North Carolina phone, or call 1-888-892-1162, for free, confidential help finding local assistance with housing, utilities, food, healthcare, and more. NC 211 is run by United Way of North Carolina, covers all 100 counties, and answers around the clock in English, Spanish, and other languages.
unemployment-insurance-idaho: Temporary weekly payments if you lost work through no fault of your own, from the Idaho Department of Labor. File online through the Claimant Portal at labor.idaho.gov, which is the fastest way, or call the claims line at 208-332-8942. You must file a weekly certification to keep payments coming.
211-illinois: Dial 2-1-1 from any Illinois phone, or text your zip code to 898211, for free, confidential help finding local assistance: housing, utilities, food, healthcare, and mental health. As of 2026, 211 covers all 102 Illinois counties around the clock.
rhode-island-wic: WIC gives healthy food, breastfeeding support, nutrition education, and health referrals to pregnant and postpartum people, infants, and children up to age 5. Rhode Island WIC runs through the RI Department of Health and local clinics. To apply, call the RI Department of Health Information Line at 401-222-5960 to reach a local clinic and set up an appointment, or start at health.ri.gov/wic.
rhode-island-medicaid-and-rite-care: Rhode Island Medicaid is free or low-cost health coverage for children, pregnant people, parents, older adults, people with disabilities, and low-income adults. RIte Care is the managed care part that covers most families and children. Rhode Island expanded Medicaid to cover low-income adults ages 19 to 64, so apply even if you were turned down before. Apply online through the HealthyRhode portal, or call HealthSource RI at 1-855-840-4774.
idaho-wic: WIC gives healthy food, breastfeeding support, nutrition education, and health referrals to pregnant and postpartum people, infants, and children up to age 5. Idaho WIC runs through local public health districts and loads benefits onto a WIC card you use at approved grocery stores. Find your nearest clinic through the WIC clinic finder on the Department of Health and Welfare site.
virginia-legal-aid-valegalaid-virginia-l: Virginia's legal aid offices provide free civil legal help to low-income residents on housing, family, public benefits, consumer, and other noncriminal matters. Call the statewide line at 1-866-534-5243 (1-866-LEGLAID) to reach the legal aid office serving your area, or find free legal information and your local office at virginialawhelp.org.
sc-thrive-free-help-applying-for-benefit: SC Thrive is a nonprofit that helps South Carolinians apply for benefits like SNAP and Healthy Connections Medicaid over the phone, at no cost. Call 1-800-726-8774 and choose Option 1 to check what you may qualify for and apply with help. Staff assist in English and Spanish, so this is a good first call if the online forms feel like too much on your own.
missouri-legal-aid-free-civil-legal-help: Missouri's legal aid offices provide free civil legal help to low-income residents on housing, family, public benefits, consumer, and other noncriminal matters. In eastern Missouri, call Legal Services of Eastern Missouri at 1-800-444-0514. In western Missouri, call Legal Aid of Western Missouri at 1-816-474-6750. Find the right office and apply at lsmo.org.
community-legal-aid-society-clasi: The Community Legal Aid Society, CLASI, provides free civil legal help to low-income Delawareans on housing, public benefits, family, immigration, disability, and elder-law matters, with offices in Wilmington, Dover, and Georgetown. Call the New Castle County office at 302-575-0660, the Kent County office in Dover at 302-674-8500, or the Sussex County office in Georgetown at 302-856-0038. For consumer, unemployment, and housing cases, Legal Services Corporation of Delaware also helps at lscd.com.
oregon-wic: WIC gives healthy food, breastfeeding support, nutrition education, and health referrals to pregnant and postpartum people, infants, and children up to age 5. Oregon WIC runs through local clinics in every county. Start with the online interest form at the Oregon Health Authority WIC site, call the state WIC office at 971-673-0040, or dial 2-1-1 to find your local clinic. You finish enrolling at an appointment with the clinic.
oklahoma-snap-food-benefits: SNAP is Oklahoma's food assistance program: monthly food money on an EBT card you use like a debit card at most grocery stores. Apply online at OKDHSLive.org, the state benefits portal that also screens you for SoonerCare, TANF, and energy help, at your local Oklahoma Human Services office, or by phone at 405-522-5050. Most applications include a phone or in-person interview, and a case can take up to 30 days.
south-dakota-liheap-low-income-energy-as: The Low Income Energy Assistance Program, LIHEAP, helps income-eligible South Dakota households pay winter heating costs and can step in for a heating emergency. Apply online through the state portal or with a paper application you email to DSSHeat@state.sd.us or mail to the Office of Energy Assistance in Pierre. Call 1-800-233-8503 to apply or check your status, Monday through Friday, 8am to 5pm Central.
iowa-wic: WIC gives healthy food, breastfeeding support, nutrition education, and health referrals to pregnant and postpartum people, infants, and children up to age 5. Iowa WIC runs through local clinics, and you set up benefits at an appointment. Find your local clinic on the Iowa WIC map, or call 1-800-972-2017 to get started.
vermont-wic: WIC gives food benefits, nutrition education, breastfeeding support, and counseling to pregnant Vermonters, new parents, and caregivers with children under 5. Vermont WIC runs through local Health Department offices, and food benefits load onto a card you use with the WICShopper app at approved stores. Apply by contacting the Vermont WIC Program at 1-800-464-4343 or 802-863-7200, by email at wic@vermont.gov, or through your local office. In-person and remote appointments are both available.
missouri-energy-assistance-liheap-and-ec: Missouri's Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program helps low-income households pay home energy bills. It has two parts: Energy Assistance, a one-time payment toward heating or cooling from October through May, and the Energy Crisis Intervention Program, ECIP, for a disconnect notice or an emergency. Apply at mydss.mo.gov or call 1-855-373-4636 to have an application mailed.
kansas-wic: WIC gives healthy food, breastfeeding support, nutrition help, and health referrals to pregnant and postpartum people, infants, and children under age 5. Kansas WIC runs through the Department of Health and Environment and local clinics. Start the online pre-application at kswic.com/PreAppPortal, find your local clinic at kdhe.ks.gov/wic, or call the state WIC office at 785-296-3683.
arizona-legal-aid-community-legal-servic: Arizona's legal aid programs give free civil legal help to low-income residents on housing, eviction, family, public benefits, and consumer problems. Community Legal Services covers Maricopa, La Paz, Mohave, Yavapai, and Yuma counties at 1-800-852-9075. For anywhere in the state, apply through AZLawHelp.org or call 1-866-637-5341 to be routed to the program serving your area.
wyoming-child-care-assistance: Child Care Assistance helps low-income Wyoming parents pay for child care while they work or attend an employment-related education program. As of August 2025 you apply through ECARES, the state's child care eligibility system. Contact your local Department of Family Services office or call 1-800-457-3659 to get started. If two parents are in the home, both must be in an approved activity during the same hours.
washington-wic: WIC gives healthy food, breastfeeding support, nutrition education, and health referrals to pregnant and postpartum people, infants, and children up to age 5. Washington WIC runs through the Department of Health and local clinics. Find a clinic or apply by calling the WIC Cascades Support Line at 1-800-841-1410, or start at doh.wa.gov.
king-outreach-ministry: King Outreach Ministry helps families in western Stokes County during a crisis. You can get food from their pantry, clothing, help with prescription medicines, and help with energy and heating costs. They can also point you to other agencies that can help.
unemployment-insurance-virginia: Temporary weekly payments if you lost work through no fault of your own, from the Virginia Employment Commission. File online through the VEC Customer Self-Service portal at vec.virginia.gov, which is the fastest way, or by phone through the Customer Contact Center at 1-866-832-2363, Monday through Friday, 8am to 4:30pm.
virginia-earned-income-tax-credit: Virginia offers two versions of the Earned Income Tax Credit, and you pick the one that helps most. One is nonrefundable and equal to 20 percent of your federal EITC. The other is refundable and, for tax years 2025 and 2026, also equal to 20 percent of your federal EITC, so it pays out even if you owe no tax. Claim it on your Virginia return.
weatherization-assistance-program-rhode-: Free home energy-efficiency work for income-eligible Rhode Island households: insulation, air sealing, and heating-system improvements that lower future bills. The RI Office of Energy Resources coordinates the program, and applications run through your local Community Action Program agency, the same agencies that take energy assistance applications. Call the Office of Energy Resources at 401-574-9117 or contact your local Community Action Program agency to start.
nebraska-energy-assistance-liheap: The Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program, LIHEAP, helps low-income Nebraska households with home energy costs. Heating help runs October 1 through March 31, cooling help runs June 1 through August 31, and crisis help is available year-round for shutoffs, reconnects, and emergencies. Apply online through iServe Nebraska, or call ACCESSNebraska at 1-800-383-4278.
maine-snap-food-supplement: SNAP, called the Food Supplement Program in Maine, puts monthly food money on an EBT card you use like a debit card at most grocery stores. Apply online through My Maine Connection at mymaineconnection.gov, the state's one application that also covers MaineCare and TANF, or by phone through the Office for Family Independence at 1-855-797-4357, Monday through Friday, 7am to 4pm.
weatherization-assistance-program-alabam: Free home energy-efficiency work for income-eligible Alabama households: an energy audit by trained staff, then improvements like air sealing and insulation that lower future bills, along with health and safety checks. The Alabama Department of Economic and Community Affairs runs the program through local agencies. Contact the agency serving your county to apply, since ADECA does not take applications directly.
missouri-wic: WIC gives healthy food, breastfeeding support, nutrition education, and health referrals to pregnant and postpartum people, infants, and children up to age 5. Missouri WIC runs through local agencies of the Department of Health and Senior Services. Call TEL-LINK at 1-800-835-5465 to find your local WIC agency, or reach the state WIC office at 1-800-392-8209.
kansas-legal-services: Kansas Legal Services provides free civil legal help to low-income Kansans on housing and eviction, family, consumer and debt, public benefits, and other noncriminal matters, across all 105 counties. Call intake at 316-267-3975, Monday through Friday, 8am to 4:30pm, or apply online at kansaslegalservices.org (the online application is open 8am Monday through 4:30pm Thursday).
unemployment-insurance-illinois-ides: Temporary weekly payments if you lost work through no fault of your own, from the Illinois Department of Employment Security. File your claim online, or call IDES Claimant Services at 1-800-244-5631. Certify for each week you claim through the automated Tele-Serve line at 1-312-338-4337.
food-assistance-program-michigan-snap: The Food Assistance Program, FAP, is Michigan's name for SNAP: monthly food money on a Bridge Card you use like a debit card at the store. Apply online through MI Bridges at newmibridges.michigan.gov, or with a paper application at your local MDHHS office.
liheap-energy-assistance: Georgia's LIHEAP helps income-qualified households pay heating and cooling bills, with crisis help for life-threatening energy emergencies. DFCS funds community action agencies that take applications; seniors 65+ and the medically homebound get an early application window.
massachusetts-earned-income-tax-credit: Massachusetts has a refundable Earned Income Tax Credit worth 40 percent of your federal EITC, raised from 30 percent for tax years starting on or after January 1, 2023. Because it is refundable, it pays out as cash even if you owe no tax. You must qualify for the federal EITC and file a Massachusetts return to claim it.
tn-211: Dial 2-1-1 from any Tennessee phone for free, confidential help finding local assistance with housing, utility bills, food, health care, and more. TN 211 is a statewide United Way service that answers around the clock, every day of the year. You can also text your ZIP code to 898-211. Details at uwtn.org/tn-211.
heap-home-energy-assistance-program: New York's help with heating and cooling bills. The Regular benefit pays a seasonal credit toward your heating cost, and separate Emergency, heating-equipment repair or replacement, and Cooling Assistance benefits handle crises. Apply at myBenefits.ny.gov or your local HEAP office; the OTDA hotline is 1-800-342-3009.
oregon-health-plan-medicaid: The Oregon Health Plan, OHP, is free health coverage for Oregonians with lower incomes: working families, children, pregnant people, single adults, and seniors. Oregon expanded Medicaid, so low-income adults 19 to 64 can qualify. Apply online through ONE at one.oregon.gov or by phone at 800-699-9075, Monday through Friday, 7am to 6pm. Members with coverage questions call 800-273-0557.
capk-vita-free-tax-preparation: Free tax preparation and e-filing for low- and moderate-income families, year-round. They can help you claim tax credits like the EITC that put real money back in your pocket.
unemployment-insurance-vermont-departmen: Vermont unemployment insurance gives short-term weekly payments if you lost work through no fault of your own, from the Vermont Department of Labor. File your initial claim online through the Claimant e-Services portal, which needs a myVermont account, or by phone at 1-800-479-6151. Wait, file by calling 1-877-214-3330, Monday through Thursday 8:30am to 4pm and Friday 9am to 4pm. For help on an existing claim, the Claimant Assistance line is 1-877-214-3332. A claim cannot start until you have actually separated from your job.
delaware-tanf-cash-assistance: Temporary Assistance for Needy Families, TANF, is Delaware's monthly cash assistance for low-income families with children. Most adults must take part in work or approved work activities for at least 30 hours a week. Apply online through Delaware ASSIST at assist.dhss.delaware.gov or at any State Service Center, then attend an interview with a DSS social worker. Call 302-255-9040 for help.
unemployment-insurance-gdol: Georgia's unemployment benefits: temporary weekly payments if you lost work through no fault of your own. File online through the Georgia Department of Labor's MyUI Claimant Portal or at a local career center; the maximum duration adjusts between 14 and 26 weeks with the state unemployment rate.
georgia-wic: Nutritious foods on an eWIC card, breastfeeding support, health education, and referrals for pregnant women, new mothers, infants, and young children in Georgia. Apply through Georgia Gateway or your county health department; call 800-228-9173 with questions.
south-carolina-wic: WIC gives healthy food, breastfeeding support, nutrition education, and health referrals to pregnant and postpartum people, infants, and children up to age 5. The South Carolina Department of Public Health runs it through local health departments. Start with the online pre-application on the DPH WIC page, or call 1-855-472-3432 to make an in-person or phone appointment.
wyoming-wic: WIC gives healthy food, breastfeeding support, nutrition education, and health referrals to pregnant and postpartum people, infants, and children under age 5. Wyoming WIC runs through local clinics of the Wyoming Department of Health. Start at health.wyo.gov/publichealth/wic, use the clinic locator to find your nearest office, or call the WIC help desk at 1-307-777-6236.
weatherization-assistance-program-south-: The Weatherization Assistance Program makes free energy-efficiency improvements for income-eligible South Dakota households: weather-stripping and sealing, adding insulation in attics, walls, and under floors, and repairing or replacing a non-working heating system so future bills drop. It runs through local community action agencies alongside energy assistance. Contact the Office of Energy Assistance at 1-800-233-8503 to get started.
massachusetts-tafdc-cash-assistance: Transitional Aid to Families with Dependent Children, TAFDC, is Massachusetts's monthly cash assistance for families with children and pregnant people in the last 120 days of pregnancy who have little or no income. It is run by the Department of Transitional Assistance. Apply online at DTAConnect.com or by phone at 1-877-382-2363. Approval also brings MassHealth automatically.
nevada-211: Dial 2-1-1 from any Nevada phone, or call 1-866-535-5654, for free, confidential help finding local assistance with housing, utilities, food, healthcare, and more. The call center answers Monday through Friday, 9am to 9pm Pacific time, and the online search and app work around the clock. You can also text your zip code to 898211.
unemployment-insurance-alaska: Unemployment Insurance pays temporary weekly benefits if you lost work through no fault of your own, from the Alaska Department of Labor and Workforce Development. The fastest way to file is online through myAlaska at my.alaska.gov. You can also reach a UI Claim Center by phone: Anchorage 907-269-4700, Fairbanks 907-451-2871, or Juneau 907-465-5552, open 10am to 3pm, Monday through Friday.
working-pennsylvanians-tax-credit: Pennsylvania's new refundable state tax credit for low- and moderate-income workers, worth 10 percent of your federal Earned Income Tax Credit, up to $805. It starts with the 2026 tax season, and if you qualify for the federal EITC you automatically qualify. Claim it on your PA-40 state return.
weatherization-assistance-program-delawa: Free home energy-efficiency work for income-eligible Delaware households: air sealing, insulation, duct and pipe sealing, and a heating-system safety check that together typically cut energy bills by 30 to 50 percent. The DNREC State Energy Office runs the program through a statewide administrator, the Energy Coordinating Agency. To apply, call the Energy Coordinating Agency at 302-504-6111; for other questions, call DNREC at 302-735-3480.
arkansas-snap-food-assistance: SNAP is Arkansas's food assistance program: monthly food money on an EBT card you use like a debit card at most grocery stores. Apply online through Access Arkansas at access.arkansas.gov, the state's one application for SNAP, Medicaid, and TEA cash assistance, or at your local Department of Human Services county office. You can also get help by phone at 1-855-372-1084.
tennessee-snap-food-assistance: SNAP is Tennessee's food assistance program: monthly food money on an EBT card you use like a debit card at most grocery stores. Apply online through the One DHS Customer Portal at onedhs.tn.gov/csp, the same portal that handles Families First cash assistance, or at your local Family Assistance office. You can also call the One DHS Contact Center at 1-833-772-8347.
dc-medicaid: DC Medicaid is free or low-cost health coverage for children, pregnant people, parents, older adults, people with disabilities, and low-income adults. The District expanded Medicaid to cover low-income adults, so apply even if you were turned down years ago. Apply online at districtdirect.dc.gov or by phone at (202) 727-5355. There is no in-person interview requirement, and it can take up to 45 days to hear back, or 60 days if you are disabled.
credit-org-free-nonprofit-credit-counsel: A nonprofit, HUD-approved agency offering free credit counseling, debt management plans, and housing counseling (including foreclosure prevention) by phone. Your first session is free with no products to sell.
wisconsin-homestead-credit: The Homestead Credit is a refundable Wisconsin credit that helps renters and homeowners with low income offset the property taxes or rent they pay. For 2025, household income must be under $24,680 to qualify (people with income at or above that must be disabled or age 62 or older). You claim it on Schedule H or H-EZ with your Wisconsin return, and it can come back as a refund even if you owe no tax.
arizona-cash-assistance-tanf: Cash Assistance is Arizona's TANF program: a modest monthly cash payment for low-income families with children, run by DES. Arizona holds adults to a lifetime limit of 12 months of Cash Assistance, one of the shortest in the country, and most adults take part in the Jobs Program. Apply online through Health-e-Arizona Plus at healthearizonaplus.gov or by phone at 1-855-432-7587.
the-salvation-army-bakersfield-corps: Free food distribution Monday through Thursday afternoons, a Tuesday senior lunch, and social services help during weekday business hours at 4417 Wilson Road.
tafi-temporary-assistance-for-families-i: TAFI is Idaho's monthly cash assistance for low-income families with children, worth up to $309 a month, with a 24-month lifetime limit for adults. Most parents take part in the Employment and Training Program while they receive it. Apply online at idalink.idaho.gov or by phone at 1-877-456-1233.
hawaii-earned-income-tax-credit: Hawaii's Earned Income Tax Credit is refundable and equal to 40 percent of the federal earned income credit you claim on your federal return. Because it is refundable, it can pay out as a refund even when it is larger than the tax you owe. Claim it on your Hawaii return using Form N-356; you must qualify for the federal EITC first.
iowa-medicaid-and-iowa-health-and-wellne: Iowa Medicaid is free or low-cost health coverage for children, pregnant people, parents, older adults, people with disabilities, and low-income adults. The Iowa Health and Wellness Plan covers low-income adults ages 19 to 64 under Medicaid expansion. Apply online through the HHS Services Portal at hhsservices.iowa.gov, or call 1-800-972-2017.
calworks-cash-aid-for-families: Monthly cash assistance plus job services and child care for California families with children in need.
washington-energy-assistance-liheap: LIHEAP helps low-income Washington households pay home heating and energy bills. The state Department of Commerce funds the program, but you apply through the local community action agency that serves your county, not through Commerce directly. Each agency sets its own appointment process, so find your local provider on the Commerce LIHEAP page and contact them to apply.
arkansas-tea-cash-assistance: Transitional Employment Assistance, TEA, is Arkansas's monthly cash assistance for low-income families with children, paired with the Work Pays employment program. Apply online through Access Arkansas at access.arkansas.gov or at your local DHS county office. TEA carries a work requirement and a time limit on how long you can receive cash, so ask your caseworker where you stand.
legal-aid-services-of-oregon: Legal Aid Services of Oregon provides free civil legal help to low-income Oregonians on housing, family, public benefits, consumer, and other noncriminal matters. For an eviction, call the statewide Eviction Defense Project at 888-585-9638. For public benefits problems, call the Public Benefits Hotline at 503-241-4111. Find your local legal aid office at lasoregon.org, and free self-help information at oregonlawhelp.org.
3squaresvt-snap-food-assistance: 3SquaresVT is Vermont's name for SNAP: monthly money for food, loaded onto a Vermont EBT card you use like a debit card at many stores and farmers markets. Apply online through the myBenefits portal, or submit a paper Form 202 by mail, at a district office, or through the document uploader. Call the Benefits Service Center at 1-800-479-6151 to apply by phone or request a form. If everyone in the home is 65 or older or gets SSI, benefits come as cash to a bank account instead of an EBT card.
wisconsin-wic: WIC gives healthy food, breastfeeding support, nutrition education, and health referrals to pregnant and postpartum people, infants, and children up to age 5. Wisconsin WIC runs through local WIC agencies. Start your pre-application online, or call the Well Badger Resource Center at 1-800-642-7837 to find your local clinic, Monday through Friday, 7am to 6pm.
capk-food-bank: Free food through more than 200 emergency food distribution sites across Kern County, plus a monthly Senior Food Box program. Call 211 to find the food distribution closest to you.
unemployment-insurance-workforce-west-vi: Temporary weekly payments if you lost work through no fault of your own, from WorkForce West Virginia. File online through the WorkForce West Virginia claims portal at uc.workforcewv.org, which is the fastest way, or get help by phone at 1-800-252-5627 (1-800-252-JOBS). You must file a claim each week to keep payments coming.
oklahoma-tanf-cash-assistance: Temporary Assistance for Needy Families, TANF, is Oklahoma's monthly cash assistance for low-income families with a minor child in the home. Adults sign a personalized TANF Work Plan aimed at getting or keeping a job, and the cash comes on a time-limited basis. Apply online at OKDHSLive.org, at your local Oklahoma Human Services office, or by phone at 405-522-5050.
weatherization-assistance-program-tennes: Free home energy-efficiency work for income-eligible Tennessee households: attic and wall insulation, air and duct sealing, and heating and cooling repairs that lower future bills. The Tennessee Housing Development Agency runs the Weatherization Assistance Program through local community agencies covering all 95 counties. Contact the agency serving your county to apply, since THDA does not take applications directly.
tennessee-legal-aid-help4tn: Tennessee's legal aid programs provide free civil legal help to low-income residents on housing and eviction, family, public benefits, consumer, and other noncriminal matters. Call the free HELP4TN legal advice line at 1-844-435-7486, which spells 1-844-HELP4TN, to be connected with a licensed Tennessee attorney, or find self-help information and your local legal aid office at help4tn.org.
wyoming-snap-food-assistance: SNAP loads monthly food money onto an EBT card you use like a debit card at most Wyoming grocery stores. Wyoming still uses a paper application: download it, then submit it to your local Department of Family Services office in person, by mail, by fax, or by email to snappowerservice@wyo.gov. For general SNAP questions call 307-473-3948, and for a scheduled interview call 1-307-777-8550.
minnesota-wic: WIC gives healthy food, breastfeeding support, nutrition education, and health referrals to pregnant and postpartum people, infants, and children up to age 5. Minnesota WIC runs through local agencies of the Minnesota Department of Health. Apply online at health.state.mn.us/wicapply, or call 1-800-942-4030 to find the WIC clinic nearest you.
washington-211: Dial 2-1-1 from any Washington phone, or call 1-877-211-9274, for free, confidential help finding local assistance with housing, utilities, food, healthcare, and more. Washington 211 is a statewide service with a database of thousands of local resources. You can also text 211WAOD to 898211 or search at wa211.org.
south-dakota-legal-aid-east-river-and-da: South Dakota's legal aid nonprofits provide free civil legal help to low-income residents on housing, family, consumer, public benefits, and other noncriminal matters. East River Legal Services covers eastern South Dakota; call 1-800-952-3015. Dakota Plains Legal Services covers western South Dakota and the tribal nations; call 605-856-4444. All three legal aid programs share one online application at sdlawhelp.org.
massachusetts-snap-food-assistance: SNAP is Massachusetts's food assistance program, run by the Department of Transitional Assistance (DTA): monthly food money on an EBT card you use like a debit card at most grocery stores. Apply online at DTAConnect.com, which takes about 20 minutes, or by phone through the DTA Assistance Line at 1-877-382-2363, press 7, open Monday through Friday, 8:15am to 4:45pm.
washington-legal-aid-clear-northwest-jus: CLEAR is Washington's toll-free legal aid intake line, run by the Northwest Justice Project, for low-income residents with civil, noncriminal problems like eviction, housing, family, and public benefits. Call 1-888-201-1014, Monday through Friday, 9:15am to 12:15pm. Residents 60 and older can call CLEAR*Sr at 1-888-387-7111. Free self-help guides are at washingtonlawhelp.org.
colorado-child-tax-credit: The Colorado Child Tax Credit is a refundable credit for lower-income families with young children, so it can come back as cash even if you owe no state tax. It is available on tax year 2025 returns for families with a child under 17 who meet the income limits. Because of state revenue rules, the credit is not offered for tax year 2026. Claim it on your Colorado return.
weatherization-assistance-program-colora: Free home energy-efficiency work for income-eligible Colorado households: insulation, air sealing, and heating-system repairs that lower future bills. The Colorado Energy Office runs the Weatherization Assistance Program through local providers across the state. Because the state office does not take applications directly, contact the weatherization provider serving your county to apply.
minnesota-legal-aid-mid-minnesota-legal-: Minnesota's legal aid programs provide free civil legal help to low-income residents on housing, family, public benefits, consumer, and other noncriminal matters. Mid-Minnesota Legal Aid also helps people age 60 and older and people with disabilities. Call 1-877-696-6529 to reach intake, and find free legal information and your local office at lawhelpmn.org.
unemployment-insurance-iowa-workforce-de: Temporary weekly payments if you lost work through no fault of your own, from Iowa Workforce Development. File your claim online at iowaworks.gov, which is the fastest way, or get help from the customer service line at 1-866-239-0843, Monday through Friday, 8am to 4:30pm.
montana-earned-income-tax-credit: Montana offers a refundable Earned Income Tax Credit equal to 10 percent of your federal EITC, so it can pay out even when it is larger than the state tax you owe. If you qualify for the federal EITC, claim the Montana credit on your state income tax return using Form 2. Free tax-preparation sites can file both returns and claim the credit at no cost.
east-stokes-outreach-ministry: East Stokes Outreach Ministry serves people in the eastern part of Stokes County, near Walnut Cove. You can get fresh food from their pantry, low-cost clothing and household items from their thrift store, and emergency financial help when times are hard.
kansas-211: Dial 2-1-1 from a Kansas phone for free, confidential help finding local assistance with rent, utilities, food, health care, and more. Kansas 211 is run statewide by United Way of the Plains and is answered Monday through Friday, 7am to 7pm, with a recorded message pointing to resources after hours. You can also text your ZIP code to 898-211 or search anytime at 211Kansas.org.
medicaid-and-chip: Free or very low-cost health coverage for people with limited income, including children (CHIP), pregnant women, seniors, and people with disabilities.
maryland-wic: WIC gives healthy food, breastfeeding support, nutrition education, and health referrals to pregnant and postpartum people, infants, and children up to age 5. Maryland WIC runs through local county offices of the Maryland Department of Health. Call 1-800-242-4942 to find your local clinic, or apply through the WIC Client Portal linked at health.maryland.gov/phpa/wic.
vermont-211: Dial 2-1-1 from any Vermont phone, or call 1-866-652-4636 (or 802-652-4636), for free, confidential help finding local assistance with housing, utilities, food, health care, and more. Vermont 211 is run by the United Ways of Vermont. You can also text your ZIP code to 898211. If you need emergency housing, call rather than text or email; emergency housing call hours are 4:30pm to 10pm on weekdays and 8am to 10pm on weekends and holidays.
wic-women-infants-and-children: Food benefits, nutrition support, and healthcare referrals for pregnant women, new mothers, and children under 5.
pennsylvania-wic: Healthy food on an eWIC card, nutrition counseling, and breastfeeding support for pregnant and postpartum people, infants, and children up to age 5. Start a pre-application online at pawic.com, or call 1-800-942-9467 to reach your closest WIC office.
montana-lieap-low-income-energy-assistan: The Low Income Energy Assistance Program, LIEAP, helps low-income Montana households pay winter heating bills and covers furnace emergencies during the heating season. Apply from October 1 through April 30 by delivering or mailing the combined LIEAP and Weatherization application to your local eligibility office. For help, call the Human and Community Services Division at 406-444-1788.
louisiana-legal-aid-louisianalawhelp-sll: Louisiana's legal aid programs give free civil legal help to low-income residents on housing, family, public benefits, and consumer matters. Find your local office and free self-help guides at louisianalawhelp.org. Southeast Louisiana Legal Services covers 22 southeast parishes and takes intake at 1-844-244-7871. Acadiana Legal Service Corporation covers much of the rest of the state.
all-kids-alabama-chip: ALL Kids is Alabama's low-cost health coverage for children under 19 in families that earn too much for Medicaid but still need affordable coverage, reaching up to 312 percent of the federal poverty level. It covers checkups, immunizations, doctor and hospital visits, prescriptions, dental, vision, and mental health care through Blue Cross Blue Shield of Alabama. Apply online or call ALL Kids at 1-888-373-5437.
south-carolina-legal-services: South Carolina Legal Services provides free civil legal help to low-income residents on housing and eviction, family, public benefits, consumer, and other noncriminal matters. Call the statewide intake line at 1-888-346-5592, or apply online at lawhelp.org/sc. A lawyer or paralegal screens your income and problem, and after you apply your local office usually contacts you within 5 to 7 business days.
unemployment-insurance-wisconsin: Temporary weekly payments if you lost work through no fault of your own, from the Wisconsin Department of Workforce Development. File online through the Claimant Portal at my.unemployment.wisconsin.gov, which is the fastest way. For help using online services, call 1-844-910-3661 (or 414-435-7069): Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, and Friday, 7:30am to 4:30pm, and Thursday, 8am to 3:15pm.
weatherization-assistance-program-south-: Free home energy-efficiency work for income-eligible South Carolina households: insulation, air sealing, and heating and cooling improvements that lower future bills and make the home safer. The Office of Economic Opportunity runs it through eight Community Action Agencies that cover all 46 counties. Contact the agency serving your county to apply; find yours at oeo.sc.gov. Both homeowners and renters can qualify.
unemployment-benefits-ohio: Temporary weekly payments if you lost work through no fault of your own, from the Ohio Department of Job and Family Services. File online at unemployment.ohio.gov, or by phone at 1-877-644-6562. The call center is open 8am to 5pm, Monday through Friday.
idaho-legal-aid-services: Idaho Legal Aid Services gives free civil legal help to low-income Idahoans on housing, family safety, public benefits, and consumer problems. Call the Legal Advice Line at 208-746-7541 to start; intake is open Monday through Wednesday only. You can also apply online and use the free self-help forms at idaholegalaid.org.
2-1-1-new-york: Dial 2-1-1 from any New York phone, or text your zip code to 898-211, for free, confidential help finding local assistance: food, rent, utility bills, health care, and more. Regional 211 centers cover all of New York State around the clock.
weatherization-assistance-program-iowa: Iowa's Weatherization Assistance Program makes free energy-efficiency improvements, like insulation and air sealing, that lower future utility bills for income-eligible households. Both homeowners and renters can qualify, with priority for older adults, people with disabilities, and families with children. Apply through your local community action agency, the same offices that run energy assistance.
colorado-leap-low-income-energy-assistan: The Low-income Energy Assistance Program, LEAP, helps low-income Colorado households pay a portion of winter home heating costs, whether you heat with gas, electric, propane, or wood. LEAP runs one season a year, November 1 through April 30. Apply online through Colorado PEAK at colorado.gov/PEAK during the season, or call 1-866-HEAT-HELP, that is 1-866-432-8435, to request a paper application or apply by phone.
south-dakota-medicaid-and-chip: South Dakota Medicaid is free or low-cost health coverage for children, pregnant people, parents, seniors, people with disabilities, and, since the state expanded Medicaid in 2023, low-income adults ages 19 to 64. CHIP covers children in families that earn a little more. Apply online through the DSS Benefits Portal at eaportal.sd.gov, or call the Department of Social Services at 605-773-3165.
state-emergency-relief-michigan-ser: State Emergency Relief helps Michigan residents through a crisis that threatens health or safety: heat and electricity shut-offs, plus rent, past-due rent, security deposits, and moving costs. Energy help has no copay for eligible households. Apply online through MI Bridges at newmibridges.michigan.gov or with form DHS-1514 at your local MDHHS office.
new-mexico-snap-food-assistance: SNAP is New Mexico's food assistance program: monthly food money on an EBT card you use like a debit card at most grocery stores. Apply online through YESNM at yes.nm.gov, the state's one application that also covers cash assistance, Medicaid, and energy help, or at your local Income Support Division (ISD) office. You can also call the Consolidated Customer Service Center at 1-800-283-4465.
wyoming-medicaid: Wyoming Medicaid is free or low-cost health coverage for children, pregnant people, parents and caretaker relatives, and people who are aged, blind, or disabled. Wyoming did not expand Medicaid, so low-income adults without children generally do not qualify no matter how little they earn. Apply online through the WES portal at wesystem.wyo.gov, or call 1-855-294-2127. If you are a child or a working parent over the limit, ask about Kid Care CHIP.
georgia-medicaid: Free or low-cost health coverage for eligible Georgia children, pregnant women, seniors, people who are blind or disabled, and some low-income parents. One Georgia Gateway application screens every Medicaid category and PeachCare for Kids together.
nj-home-energy-assistance-liheap-and-usf: New Jersey runs two energy bill programs off one application through the DCAid portal. The Universal Service Fund, USF, gives a monthly credit on gas and electric bills year round. LIHEAP helps with heating and cooling costs on a seasonal schedule. Apply at dcaid.dca.nj.gov, or call the energy assistance hotline at 1-800-510-3102.
unemployment-insurance-utah: Temporary weekly payments if you lost work through no fault of your own, from the Utah Department of Workforce Services. File online at jobs.utah.gov/ui, which is the fastest way, or call the claims center. The statewide line for counties outside the Wasatch Front is 1-888-848-0688. You must file a weekly claim to keep payments coming.
maryland-medicaid-healthchoice-and-mchp: Maryland Medicaid is free or low-cost health coverage for children, pregnant people, parents, older adults, people with disabilities, and low-income adults. Most members get care through HealthChoice, Maryland's Medicaid managed care program, and MCHP covers children through CHIP. Apply through Maryland Health Connection at marylandhealthconnection.gov, or call 1-855-642-8572, Monday through Friday, 8am to 6pm.
temporary-assistance-family-assistance-a: New York's cash assistance for people who can't meet basic needs. Family Assistance helps families with children and carries a 60-month lifetime limit on federally funded aid; Safety Net Assistance covers single adults, childless couples, and families who have used up Family Assistance. Apply at myBenefits.ny.gov or your local social services district.
tanf-cash-assistance-2: Pennsylvania's cash help for low-income families with children, paid on the EBT ACCESS card. Adults are limited to 60 months of TANF in a lifetime, though Extended TANF can continue benefits in specific hardship situations. Apply at COMPASS or your county assistance office.
nevada-medicaid-and-nevada-check-up: Nevada Medicaid is free or low-cost health coverage for children, pregnant people, parents, older adults, people with disabilities, and low-income adults. Nevada Check Up covers children through CHIP. Nevada expanded Medicaid, so low-income adults 19 to 64 can qualify too. Apply online through Access Nevada at accessnevada.nv.gov, which has a pre-screening tool, or at a local welfare office. Call 775-684-0800 with questions.
weatherization-assistance-program-oklaho: Free home energy-efficiency work for income-eligible Oklahoma households: air sealing, insulation, weather-stripping, and heating-system repairs that lower future bills. The Oklahoma Department of Commerce runs the program through local Community Action Agencies. Contact the Community Action Agency serving your county to apply, since Commerce does not take applications directly.
mississippi-liheap-home-energy-assistanc: LIHEAP helps low-income Mississippi households pay heating and cooling bills and handle an energy crisis. Apply online through the Access MS portal at access.ms.gov and pick Community Services; your local Community Action Agency then processes the case and schedules an appointment. It runs in all 82 counties as funds last. Call the MDHS Community Services Division at 1-800-421-0762.
vermont-earned-income-tax-credit: Vermont's Earned Income Tax Credit is a refundable credit equal to 38 percent of your federal EITC, so it can pay out as cash even when it is larger than the tax you owe. You claim it on Schedule IN-112 with your Vermont income tax return. In Vermont, the credit is open to all qualifying residents regardless of whether you, your spouse, or a qualifying child has a Social Security number, so filers using an ITIN can claim it. Free VITA tax help can file your federal and Vermont returns and claim both credits at no cost.
child-care-assistance-program-louisiana-: The Child Care Assistance Program, CCAP, helps eligible Louisiana families pay for child care so parents can work, go to school, or train. The Louisiana Department of Education runs it. Apply through the CAFE portal at cafe-cp.doe.louisiana.gov or by paper application, or call 1-877-453-2721 for help.
snap-food-assistance-ohio: Ohio SNAP loads monthly food money on the Ohio Direction Card, which works like a debit card at grocery stores. Apply online through Ohio Benefits at benefits.ohio.gov, by phone at 1-844-640-6446, or at your County Department of Job and Family Services.
new-mexico-liheap-energy-assistance: LIHEAP, the Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program, helps eligible New Mexico households with heating and cooling costs. Apply online through YESNM at yes.nm.gov, at your local Income Support Division office, or with a paper form the state offers in English, Spanish, Vietnamese, and Simplified Chinese. Call 1-800-283-4465 with questions, and include a disconnect notice if a shut-off is coming.
new-mexico-working-families-tax-credit: The Working Families Tax Credit is New Mexico's version of the Earned Income Tax Credit, and it is refundable, so it can pay out as cash even if you owe no tax. For tax year 2023 and after, the credit equals 25 percent of your federal Earned Income Tax Credit, up from 20 percent in 2022. Claim it on your New Mexico personal income tax return, Form PIT-1.
florida-kidcare: Health and dental insurance for Florida children from birth through age 18, combining Medicaid for children, MediKids, Florida Healthy Kids, and the Children's Medical Services plan. Most families pay $15 or $20 a month; many pay nothing.
iowa-family-investment-program-fip-cash-: The Family Investment Program, FIP, is Iowa's version of TANF: monthly cash assistance for low-income families with children. Most adults take part in PROMISE JOBS, the work and training side of the program. Apply online through Iowa's HHS Services Portal at hhsservices.iowa.gov or at your local Iowa HHS office.
idaho-medicaid-expanded-coverage: Idaho Medicaid is free or low-cost health coverage for children, pregnant people, parents, seniors, people with disabilities, and low-income adults. Idaho voters approved Medicaid expansion in 2018, and coverage for low-income adults began in 2020. Apply online at idalink.idaho.gov or by phone at 1-877-456-1233.
oregon-snap-food-benefits: SNAP is Oregon's food benefit program: monthly food money loaded onto an Oregon Trail Card (EBT) you use like a debit card at most grocery stores. Apply online through ONE at one.oregon.gov, at a local Oregon Department of Human Services office, or by phone at 800-699-9075, Monday through Friday, 7am to 6pm. One ONE application also checks you for the Oregon Health Plan, TANF cash, and child care help.
louisiana-earned-income-tax-credit: Louisiana has a refundable state Earned Income Tax Credit worth 5 percent of your federal EITC. Because it is refundable, it can pay out as cash even if you owe no state income tax. You must qualify for the federal EITC first, then claim the Louisiana credit on Line 16 of your Louisiana IT-540 return.
husky-health-connecticut-medicaid-and-ch: HUSKY Health is Connecticut's Medicaid and CHIP program: free or low-cost coverage. HUSKY A covers children, parents, caretakers, and pregnant people; HUSKY B is CHIP for children; HUSKY C covers adults 65 and older and people with disabilities; HUSKY D covers low-income adults under 65. Enroll through Access Health CT at 1-855-805-4325, Monday through Friday, 8am to 4pm, or apply through ConneCT.
montana-legal-services-association-monta: Montana Legal Services Association gives free civil legal help to low-income Montanans on housing, family, public benefits, consumer, and other noncriminal matters. Call the HELP Line at 1-800-666-6899, open Tuesday through Thursday, 9am to 1pm, or find free legal information, forms, and your local provider at montanalawhelp.org.
housing-authority-of-the-county-of-kern: Runs Section 8 Housing Choice Vouchers, Project-Based Vouchers, and affordable housing communities across Kern County. Some waiting lists open and close during the year, so check which programs are accepting applications.
kentucky-211: Dial 2-1-1 from any Kentucky phone for free, confidential help finding local assistance with food, housing, utility bills, healthcare, and more. Kentucky 211 is a United Way service that answers around the clock, every day. You can also text your zip code to 898211 or search at kentucky211.org.
montana-elderly-homeowner-renter-credit: The Montana Elderly Homeowner/Renter Credit is a refundable credit of up to 1,150 dollars that helps older Montanans with the property taxes or rent they paid on their home. You may qualify if you were 62 or older at the end of the year and had total household income under 45,000 dollars. Both homeowners and renters claim it on Form 2 with Schedule 2EC, even if you do not otherwise have to file.
utah-chip-childrens-health-insurance: Utah CHIP is low-cost health coverage for uninsured children and teens whose family earns too much for Medicaid but still needs help paying for care. It covers checkups, doctor visits, dental, vision, and prescriptions. Apply online through myCase at jobs.utah.gov/mycase, the same application used for Medicaid, or call 1-877-543-7669, which spells 1-877-KIDS-NOW.
delaware-211: Dial 2-1-1 from any Delaware phone, or call 1-800-560-3372, for free, confidential help finding local assistance with housing, utilities, food, healthcare, and more. You can also text your ZIP code to 898-211. Delaware 211 is staffed Monday through Friday, 8am to 7pm, and it refers you to local programs rather than paying bills itself.
weatherization-assistance-program-michig: Free home energy-efficiency work for income-eligible Michigan households: insulation, air sealing, and heating-system repairs that lower future bills. MDHHS runs the program through local Community Action Agencies. Contact the Community Action Agency serving your area to apply.
liheap-energy-assistance-south-carolina: The Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program, LIHEAP, helps eligible South Carolina households pay home heating and cooling bills and covers energy crises. The Office of Economic Opportunity funds it, but you apply through the Community Action Agency serving your county, not through a central office. Find your local agency at oeo.sc.gov or dial 2-1-1. Application periods are seasonal and funds are limited, so ask your agency for the current open dates.
texas-wic: Healthy foods, breastfeeding support, and nutrition help for pregnant women, new mothers, and children under 5 in Texas. Apply online or find a local WIC office; benefits start at pregnancy and continue until a child turns 5.
healthy-louisiana-louisiana-medicaid-and: Healthy Louisiana is the state's Medicaid program: free or low-cost health coverage for children, pregnant people, parents, older adults, people with disabilities, and low-income adults. Louisiana expanded Medicaid, so adults 19 to 64 with income up to 138 percent of the federal poverty level can qualify. LaCHIP covers children. Apply at MyMedicaid.la.gov, or call Louisiana Medicaid at 1-888-342-6207, Monday through Friday, 8am to 4:30pm.
louisiana-fitap-cash-assistance: The Family Independence Temporary Assistance Program, FITAP, is Louisiana's monthly cash assistance for low-income families with children. Most work-eligible adults take part in the STEP program (Strategies to Empower People), which pairs work activities with support like child care and transportation. Apply online through the CAFE Self-Service Portal or by phone at 1-888-524-3578. Federal and state time limits apply.
weatherization-assistance-program-utah: Utah's Weatherization Assistance Program makes free energy-efficiency improvements, insulation, air sealing, and heating-system repairs, so your utility bills drop over time. The Division of Housing and Community Development runs it through local agencies across the state, and you apply to the agency serving your county. Households save an average of about 583 dollars a year, and you can ask for a weatherization referral when you apply for HEAT.
south-dakota-housing-rental-assistance: South Dakota Housing helps income-eligible renters through the Housing Choice Voucher, also called Section 8, which pays part of your monthly rent, plus security deposit assistance and other programs. There is no open pandemic-era emergency rental assistance program right now, so for a rent crisis dial 2-1-1 for local funds. Call South Dakota Housing at 1-800-540-4241 to ask about vouchers and current waitlists.
snap-food-stamps-illinois: Illinois SNAP loads monthly food money on the Illinois Link card, which works like a debit card at grocery stores. Apply online at ABE (abe.illinois.gov), by phone, or at your local Family Community Resource Center. The DHS Help Line is 1-800-843-6154.
washington-tanf-workfirst-cash-assistanc: Temporary Assistance for Needy Families, TANF, is Washington's monthly cash assistance for low-income families with children. Most adults take part in WorkFirst, the state's employment program, while the cash steadies the household. Apply online at washingtonconnection.org or by phone at 1-877-501-2233, or at your local DSHS Community Services Office.
nj-211: Dial 2-1-1 from any New Jersey phone for free, confidential help finding local assistance with housing, utilities, food, healthcare, and legal services. NJ 211 is a statewide nonprofit that answers around the clock, every day, in many languages. You can also text your zip code to 898211 or search at nj211.org.
temporary-family-assistance-tfa-cash-ass: Temporary Family Assistance, TFA, is Connecticut's monthly cash assistance for low-income families with children, the state's part of the federal TANF program. Most adults take part in Jobs First, which pairs the cash with employment services. Apply online through ConneCT at connect.ct.gov or at your local Department of Social Services office.
unemployment-insurance-connecticut-dol: Temporary weekly payments if you lost work through no fault of your own, from the Connecticut Department of Labor. File online through ReEmployCT, the state's unemployment system, which is the fastest way. If you need help, the Consumer Contact Center is 1-800-956-3294, Monday through Friday, 7:30am to 4:30pm.
211-kern-county: Kern County's local 211 line, run by CAPK. Free, confidential referrals to rent help, shelters, food, utility assistance, and more, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
capk-veterans-and-supportive-services: Housing help for veterans and their families: rental assistance to prevent homelessness (SSVF), short-term and transitional housing, and permanent supportive housing. Case managers walk with you through the whole process.
minnesota-energy-assistance-program-eap: The Energy Assistance Program helps income-qualified Minnesota households pay home heating and electric bills and covers emergencies like a broken furnace or a shutoff. Both homeowners and renters can apply. The program runs each year from October 1 through May 31 through the local service provider for your county. To find your provider, call the Commerce Energy Information Center at 1-800-657-3710.
colorado-works-tanf-cash-assistance: Colorado Works is the state's Temporary Assistance for Needy Families, TANF, program: monthly cash assistance for low-income families with a child in the home, paired with job training and employment support. Apply online through Colorado PEAK at colorado.gov/PEAK or at your county human services office. Counties run the program and have up to 45 days to process a completed application.
dc-health-care-alliance: The DC Health Care Alliance is a locally funded program that provides medical coverage to District residents who are not eligible for Medicaid, have no other health insurance, and are not eligible for Medicare. Because federal Medicaid requires a qualifying immigration status, Alliance is often the coverage route for residents who cannot get Medicaid for that reason. Alliance and the Immigrant Children's Program combined into one program, Health Care Alliance for Adults and Children. Apply the same way as Medicaid, online at districtdirect.dc.gov or by phone at (202) 727-5355.
seasonal-fuel-assistance-vermont-liheap: Seasonal Fuel Assistance is Vermont's LIHEAP program, and it pays a portion of your winter home heating bills whether you own or rent and whether you pay for heat directly or as part of your rent. Apply online through the myBenefits portal, in person at your district office, or by calling 1-800-479-6151 to request a paper application. If you got Fuel Assistance last season, watch for the annual review form instead. Once you are an active Seasonal Fuel household, you also qualify for free weatherization.
kancare-kansas-medicaid-and-chip: KanCare is Kansas's Medicaid and CHIP program: free or low-cost health coverage for children, pregnant people, low-income parents, older adults, and people with disabilities. Kansas has not expanded Medicaid, so most adults without children or a disability do not qualify no matter how low their income. Apply at ApplyForKanCare.ks.gov, or call the KanCare Clearinghouse at 1-800-792-4884.
florida-wic: Free healthy foods, breastfeeding support, nutrition education, and referrals for pregnant and postpartum women, infants, and children under 5 in Florida. Apply through your county health department; being on Medicaid, SNAP, or TANF qualifies you automatically on income.
michigan-wic: WIC gives healthy food, breastfeeding support, nutrition education, and health referrals to pregnant and postpartum women, infants, and children up to age 5. Michigan WIC is offered through county health departments and local agencies. Call 800-942-1636 to find your local clinic, or find one at Signupwic.com.
hawaii-wic: WIC gives healthy supplemental foods on an eWIC card, plus nutrition education, breastfeeding support, and health referrals for pregnant, postpartum, and breastfeeding women, and for infants and children under age 5. Hawaii WIC runs through the Department of Health. Apply online at hiwic.org and find your nearest clinic. For information, call the WIC Info Line at 808-586-4400.
tanf-cash-assistance: Monthly cash for very-low-income Georgia families with children under 18, and pregnant women. Apply at gateway.ga.gov or by paper Form 297 to your county DFCS office; adults are limited to 48 months in a lifetime.
snap-food-stamps-georgia-gateway: Georgia SNAP puts monthly grocery money on an EBT card. Apply through Georgia Gateway at gateway.ga.gov, where one account also handles Medicaid, TANF, WIC, and child care assistance, or call DFCS at 877-423-4746.
crisis-intervention-program-north-caroli: The Crisis Intervention Program helps when you are in or about to be in a heating or cooling emergency, such as a disconnect notice or no working heat or air. Unlike LIEAP, it runs year-round and covers both heating and cooling. Apply at your county Department of Social Services by mail, email, fax, or drop-off.
unemployment-insurance-nys-dol: Temporary weekly payments if you lost work through no fault of your own. File your first claim online through your NY.gov ID at the Department of Labor, or by phone with the Telephone Claims Center at 1-888-209-8124, Monday through Friday 8am to 5pm.
alaska-snap-food-assistance: SNAP is Alaska's food assistance program: monthly food money loaded onto an Alaska Quest EBT card you use like a debit card at most grocery stores. The fastest way to apply is online through the Alaska Connect portal, linked from the Division of Public Assistance SNAP page. You can also apply by phone through the Virtual Contact Center at 800-478-7778 (TDD or Alaska Relay 7-1-1) or at a local Public Assistance office.
mississippi-child-care-payment-program-c: CCPP helps eligible working parents pay for child care through a certificate to a licensed provider, and families pay a monthly co-payment set by family size and income. MDHS fills open slots from a waitlist, so add your email to the waitlist to get a personalized application link. Questions go to 1-800-877-7882.
hud-housing-counseling: Free or low-cost HUD-approved counselors who help with eviction prevention, foreclosure, renting, and homelessness — and know every local housing program.
arizona-nutrition-assistance-snap: Nutrition Assistance is what Arizona calls SNAP: monthly food money on an EBT card you use like a debit card at most grocery stores. The Department of Economic Security (DES) runs it. Apply online through Health-e-Arizona Plus at healthearizonaplus.gov, which also covers AHCCCS health coverage and Cash Assistance on one application, or call 1-855-432-7587.
nevada-child-care-subsidy-child-care-and: Nevada's Child Care and Development Program helps low-income working families pay for child care so a parent can work or go to school. The Division of Welfare and Supportive Services runs it, and you apply through Access Nevada at accessnevada.nv.gov. For questions about the program, call 775-684-0625.
north-dakota-tanf-cash-assistance: Temporary Assistance for Needy Families, TANF, is North Dakota's monthly cash assistance for low-income families with children. Most adults take part in the JOBS program, Job Opportunities and Basic Skills, which helps you move toward work. Apply online through the Self Service Portal at applyforhelp.nd.gov or by phone through the HHS Customer Support Center at 1-866-614-6005.
north-dakota-snap-food-assistance: SNAP is North Dakota's food assistance program: monthly food money on an EBT card you use like a debit card at most grocery stores. Apply online through the state Self Service Portal at applyforhelp.nd.gov, which handles SNAP, Medicaid, LIHEAP, TANF, and child care on one application, or by phone through the HHS Customer Support Center at 1-866-614-6005.
the-open-door-network: Shelter and support for people facing homelessness, domestic violence, sexual assault, or human trafficking in Kern County. Their crisis hotline answers 24 hours a day.
new-mexico-211: Dial 2-1-1 from any New Mexico phone for free, confidential help finding local assistance with housing, utilities, food, healthcare, and more. The service is run by United Way and routes your call by where you live. In the Albuquerque and Santa Fe area, United Way of North Central New Mexico answers direct at 505-245-1735, Monday through Friday, 8am to 5pm.
virginia-medicaid-cardinal-care-and-fami: Virginia Medicaid, known as Cardinal Care, is free or low-cost health coverage for children, pregnant people, parents, older adults, people with disabilities, and low-income adults. FAMIS covers children through CHIP. Apply online through CommonHelp, or call the Cover Virginia Call Center at 1-855-242-8282, Monday through Friday, 8am to 7pm.
kansas-food-assistance-snap: Food Assistance is Kansas's name for SNAP: monthly food money on a Kansas Benefits Card you use like a debit card at most grocery stores. The Department for Children and Families runs it. Apply through the DCF Self-Service Portal at cssp.kees.ks.gov, at your local DCF service center, or by phone. Call Benefits Assistance at 1-888-369-4777 or the DCF Customer Service Center at 1-833-765-2003.
tenncare-medicaid-and-coverkids-chip: TennCare is Tennessee's Medicaid program: free or low-cost health coverage for eligible children, pregnant women, low-income parents and caretakers, older adults, and people with disabilities. CoverKids is Tennessee's CHIP, covering children and pregnant women who earn a little too much for TennCare Medicaid. Apply online through TennCare Connect at tenncareconnect.tn.gov, or call 1-855-259-0701.
mass-211: Dial 2-1-1 from any Massachusetts phone, or call 1-877-211-6277, for free, confidential help finding local assistance with housing, utilities, food, healthcare, and more. Mass 211 answers around the clock, every day, with information in more than 150 languages. You can also chat or search the resource directory at mass211.org.
kentucky-snap-food-assistance: SNAP is Kentucky's food assistance program: monthly food money loaded onto an EBT card you use like a debit card at most grocery stores. Apply online through kynect at kynect.ky.gov, by phone at 1-855-306-8959, or at your local Department for Community Based Services (DCBS) office. The DCBS Family Support line answers Monday through Friday, 8am to 4:30pm Eastern.
care-fera-utility-bill-discounts: 30-35% discount on electricity and 20% on gas bills from PG&E, SCE, SoCalGas, and SDG&E for income-qualified households. Enrollment is a short form with your utility.
caleitc-young-child-tax-credit: Cash-back state tax credits worth hundreds to thousands of dollars for low-income workers — even if you owe no taxes. Free tax prep available.
nebraska-medicaid-heritage-health: Nebraska Medicaid is free or low-cost health coverage for children, pregnant people, parents, older adults, people with disabilities, and low-income adults. Most members get care through Heritage Health managed care plans. Nebraska expanded Medicaid, and the Heritage Health Adult program now covers low-income adults 19 to 64. Apply online through iServe Nebraska at iserve.nebraska.gov.
arkids-first-childrens-health-coverage: ARKids First is Arkansas's health coverage for children, combining Medicaid as ARKids A and CHIP as ARKids B so kids get checkups, shots, dental, vision, and hospital care. Apply online through Access Arkansas at access.arkansas.gov, or call 1-855-372-1084. Children can qualify even when a parent does not.
general-assistance-kern-county-dhs: Cash help with rent, utilities, transportation, and personal needs for adults with no other means of support. A Disability Advocate can also help you apply for SSI if you have a long-term disability.
weatherization-assistance-program-arkans: The Weatherization Assistance Program makes free energy-efficiency repairs, insulation, air sealing, and heating and cooling fixes, so your utility bills drop over time. Income-eligible homeowners and renters both qualify. Arkansas delivers it through local community action agencies, so contact the agency serving your county through the Arkansas Community Action Agencies Association at acaaa.org, or call 501-372-0807.
nevada-legal-aid-nevada-legal-services-a: Nevada's legal aid offices provide free civil legal help to low-income residents on housing, eviction, family, public benefits, consumer, and other noncriminal matters. Nevada Legal Services serves the whole state from offices in Las Vegas, Reno, Carson City, and Elko; call its toll-free line at 1-866-432-0404. In Clark County, the Legal Aid Center of Southern Nevada also helps at 702-386-1070.
weatherization-assistance-program-new-je: Free home energy-efficiency work for income-eligible New Jersey households: insulation, air sealing, and heating-system improvements that lower future bills. The Department of Community Affairs runs the program through local agencies. Apply through the DCAid portal at dcaid.dca.nj.gov, or contact the WAP agency that serves your county.
foodshare-wisconsin-snap: FoodShare is Wisconsin's SNAP program: monthly food money on a QUEST EBT card you use like a debit card at most grocery stores.
