Apply online through ACCESS at access.wisconsin.gov, which handles FoodShare, BadgerCare Plus, and other programs on one application, or through your local county or tribal agency. You can also manage your case with the MyACCESS app. For help, call ForwardHealth Member Services at 1-800-362-3002, Monday through Friday, 8am to 6pm.
unemployment-insurance-nebraska: Temporary weekly payments if you lost work through no fault of your own, from the Nebraska Department of Labor. File your claim online through NEworks at neworks.nebraska.gov, which is how Nebraska takes unemployment claims. Set up your NEworks account, file your initial claim, then file a weekly claim each week to keep payments coming.
wv-works-tanf-cash-assistance: WV WORKS is West Virginia's Temporary Assistance for Needy Families program, giving monthly cash assistance to eligible families with children. It pairs the cash with work and education activities like job skills training, vocational training, and college. Apply online through wvPATH at wvpath.wv.gov or at your local Department of Human Services field office. Most families on WV WORKS also receive SNAP and Medicaid.
summer-utility-shutoff-protection-arizon: Arizona bars its regulated electric utilities from disconnecting your power during the hottest months. Under Arizona Corporation Commission rules, companies like Arizona Public Service, Tucson Electric Power, and UNS Electric cannot shut off service from June 1 through October 15, or when high heat is forecast. Your bill still adds up during the moratorium, so call your utility about a payment plan and apply for LIHEAP. To report a wrongful disconnection, call ACC Consumer Services at 1-800-222-7000.
family-independence-program-michigan-cas: The Family Independence Program, FIP, is Michigan's TANF cash assistance for low-income families with children, paid monthly on the Bridge Card. Adults have a 60-month lifetime limit, and applicants take part in the PATH work program. Apply online through MI Bridges at newmibridges.michigan.gov or at your local MDHHS office.
nj-snap-food-assistance: NJ SNAP is New Jersey's name for food stamps: monthly food money on a Families First EBT card you use like a debit card at most grocery stores and some farmers markets. Apply online through the state's NJ One App, which also covers cash assistance and NJ FamilyCare, or at your county social service agency.
liheap-energy-assistance-tennessee: LIHEAP, the Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program, helps low-income Tennessee households pay home heating and cooling bills. The Tennessee Housing Development Agency, THDA, runs it through a network of local community action agencies that reach all 95 counties. Payments go straight to your utility company. Apply online at thda.org/liheap or through the agency serving your county.
211-south-dakota-helpline-center: Dial 2-1-1, or call 605-339-4357, to reach the Helpline Center for free, confidential help finding local assistance with food, housing, utilities, healthcare, and more across South Dakota. The Helpline Center is a round-the-clock resource, and its specialists search for programs near you while you are on the line. You can also search at helplinecenter.org.
iowa-earned-income-tax-credit: Iowa offers a refundable Earned Income Tax Credit worth 15 percent of your federal EITC. Because it is refundable, it pays out as cash even if you owe no state tax. Claim it on your Iowa income tax return after you qualify for the federal credit.
arizona-medicaid-ahcccs: AHCCCS, the Arizona Health Care Cost Containment System, is the state's Medicaid program: free or low-cost health coverage for children, pregnant people, parents, older adults, people with disabilities, and low-income adults. Apply online through Health-e-Arizona Plus at healthearizonaplus.gov, or call 1-855-432-7587 to apply by phone.
masshealth-medicaid-and-childrens-medica: MassHealth is Massachusetts's Medicaid and CHIP program: free or low-cost health coverage for children, pregnant people, parents, older adults, people with disabilities, and low-income adults. The Children's Medical Security Plan covers uninsured children under 19 who do not qualify for MassHealth, regardless of immigration status. Apply online or call MassHealth Customer Service at 1-800-841-2900, Monday through Friday, 8am to 5pm.
tennessee-wic: WIC gives healthy food, breastfeeding support, nutrition education, and health referrals to pregnant and postpartum women, infants, and children up to age 5. Tennessee WIC runs through county health departments and local clinics. Call 1-800-342-5942, which spells 1-800-DIAL-WIC, to find your local clinic and start, or visit tn.gov/health/wic.
medi-cal-california-medicaid: Free or low-cost health coverage for low-income Californians — doctor visits, prescriptions, mental health, and dental for most members.
211-rhode-island-united-way-of-rhode-isl: Dial 2-1-1 from any Rhode Island phone, or call 401-519-0360, for free, confidential help finding local assistance with housing, utilities, food, child care, healthcare, and more. 211 Rhode Island is run by United Way of Rhode Island and answers around the clock, every day of the year, with translation available in many languages. You can also chat with a resource specialist online.
mo-healthnet-missouri-medicaid: MO HealthNet is Missouri's Medicaid program: free or low-cost health coverage for children, pregnant people, parents, older adults, people with disabilities, and low-income adults. Missouri expanded Medicaid, so adults ages 19 to 64 can now qualify. Apply online at mydss.mo.gov or by phone at 1-855-373-9994. General MO HealthNet questions go to 1-800-392-2161.
unemployment-insurance-oklahoma-oesc: Weekly unemployment payments if you lost work through no fault of your own, from the Oklahoma Employment Security Commission, OESC. File online through the OESC Claimant Portal at claimantportal.oesc.ok.gov, which is the fastest way, or reach the unemployment support line at 405-525-1500 for help.
weatherization-assistance-program-arizon: Free home energy-efficiency work for income-eligible Arizona households: insulation, air sealing, and heating and cooling improvements that lower future bills and make the home safer in extreme heat. The Arizona Department of Housing runs it through local providers. Apply by contacting the weatherization provider for your county, listed on the Department of Housing program page.
oregon-kids-credit: The Oregon Kids Credit is a refundable state tax credit worth up to $1,050 for each qualifying child age 5 or younger, for up to five children. For the 2025 tax year the full credit goes to families with modified adjusted gross income of $26,550 or less, and it phases out completely at $31,550. Because it is refundable, it pays out even if you owe no Oregon tax. Claim it on your Oregon return.
arkansas-wic: WIC gives healthy food, breastfeeding support, nutrition education, and health referrals to pregnant and postpartum people, infants, and children up to age 5. Arkansas WIC runs through local health units of the Arkansas Department of Health. Apply through your local health unit, or call the state WIC office at 501-661-2508 for the clinic nearest you.
legal-aid-society-of-hawaii: The Legal Aid Society of Hawaii provides free civil legal help to low-income residents statewide on housing and eviction, public benefits, family, elder, and consumer matters. It does not handle criminal or personal injury cases. Call the intake line at 808-536-4302 on Oahu, or 1-800-499-4302 from the neighbor islands, Monday through Friday from 9:00 to 11:30am and 1:00 to 3:30pm. You can also start an application through online intake.
families-first-tennessee-tanf-cash-assis: Families First is Tennessee's Temporary Assistance for Needy Families, TANF, program: monthly cash assistance for low-income families with children, paired with a Personal Responsibility Plan that can include work, training, education, child care help, and transportation support. Apply online through the One DHS Customer Portal at onedhs.tn.gov/csp or at your local Family Assistance office. You can also call 1-833-772-8347.
unemployment-insurance-dc-does: Temporary weekly payments if you lost work through no fault of your own, from the DC Department of Employment Services, DOES. File your claim online through DCNetworks at dcnetworks.org, which is the fastest way, or get help by phone at (202) 724-7000, toll-free at 1-877-319-7346, Monday through Friday, 8:30am to 4:30pm.
louisiana-211: Dial 2-1-1 from any Louisiana phone for free, confidential help finding local assistance with housing, utilities, food, healthcare, and more. Louisiana 211 answers around the clock, every day, with live specialists and interpreters. You can also text your zip code to 898211 or search at louisiana211.org.
unemployment-compensation-pa-l-and-i: Temporary weekly payments if you lost work through no fault of your own. File your initial claim online at the Department of Labor and Industry, or by phone with the UC Service Center at 1-888-313-7284, Monday through Friday 8am to 4pm. File weekly certifications through PA Teleclaims.
ohio-wic: Healthy food, nutrition education, and breastfeeding support for pregnant and postpartum women, infants, and children up to age 5. WIC clinics operate in all 88 Ohio counties. Call the Help Me Grow Helpline at 1-800-755-4769 to find your local clinic.
reach-up-vermont-tanf-cash-assistance: Reach Up is Vermont's monthly cash assistance for families with minor, dependent children, paired with case management to help you reach goals around work, education, housing, health, and more. Apply online, in person at your local district office, or by calling 1-800-479-6151 to request a paper application. You take part in an interview by phone or in person. If the child's other parent lives elsewhere, a child support case usually opens automatically unless you request a safety waiver.
maryland-earned-income-tax-credit: Maryland offers a state Earned Income Tax Credit on top of the federal credit, and part of it is refundable, so it can pay out even if you owe no tax. The nonrefundable state credit equals 50 percent of your federal EITC, and the refundable credit equals 45 percent of your federal EITC. Claim it on your Maryland return at marylandtaxes.gov.
weatherization-assistance-program-virgin: Free home energy-efficiency work for income-eligible Virginia households: insulation, air sealing, and heating-system improvements that lower future bills. The Department of Housing and Community Development runs the program through local providers. Contact the weatherization provider serving your area to apply, since DHCD does not take applications directly.
south-dakota-wic: WIC gives healthy food, breastfeeding support, nutrition education, and health referrals to pregnant and postpartum people, infants, and children up to age 5. South Dakota WIC runs through the Department of Health. Apply at sd.gov/wic, or call the Department of Health at 605-773-3361 to find your local WIC clinic.
nebraska-wic: WIC gives healthy food at no cost, breastfeeding support, nutrition education, and health referrals to pregnant and postpartum people, infants, and children up to age 5. Nebraska WIC runs through local clinics across the state. Find your nearest clinic on the DHHS WIC locator, then call it to book an in-person appointment.
township-trustee-emergency-assistance-po: Every Indiana township has a trustee who by law provides emergency poor relief to residents in need: help with rent to stop an eviction, a utility bill to prevent a shutoff, food, clothing, and sometimes burial costs. Help usually comes as a voucher paid to the landlord or utility, not cash. You apply at the trustee's office for the township where you live. Find yours through your county website or the Indiana Township Association at ita-in.org.
unemployment-compensation-alabama: Temporary weekly payments if you lost work through no fault of your own, from the Alabama Department of Labor. File online through the Claimant Portal at uiclaimantportal.labor.alabama.gov, which is the fastest way. For questions about a claim's eligibility, call 1-855-234-2856.
montana-wic: WIC gives healthy food, breastfeeding support, nutrition education, and health referrals to pregnant and postpartum people, infants, and children up to age 5. To start, find a clinic and prescreen at signupwic.com, or call 1-844-583-3237. A father, grandparent, foster parent, or guardian raising a child under 5 can apply for that child.
mississippi-center-for-legal-services-so: Free civil legal help for low-income residents of southern Mississippi on housing, family, public benefits, consumer, and other noncriminal matters. Call the intake hotline at 1-800-519-2915. You can also find free legal information and your local office at mslegalservices.org.
maine-earned-income-tax-credit: Maine's Earned Income Credit is refundable and equal to 25 percent of your federal Earned Income Tax Credit, or 50 percent for workers with no qualifying children. Because it is refundable for Maine residents and part-year residents, it can pay out as cash even if you owe no state tax. Claim it on Form 1040ME, Schedule A. Questions go to Maine Revenue Services at income.tax@maine.gov.
211-maryland: Dial 2-1-1 from any Maryland phone for free, confidential help finding local assistance with housing, utilities, food, healthcare, and more. 211 Maryland is a statewide service that answers around the clock, every day of the year. You can also text your keyword to 898-211 for ongoing support, or search at 211md.org.
weatherization-assistance-program-hawaii: The Weatherization Assistance Program (WAP) makes free energy-efficiency improvements so your utility bill shrinks, based on a home energy audit. Measures can include high-efficiency faucet aerators and shower heads, LED lighting, and an energy-efficient solar water heater, all at no cost. On Oahu the program is run by the Honolulu Community Action Program (HCAP), funded by the U.S. Department of Energy and the Hawaii State Office of Community Services. Neighbor-island households apply through their county Community Action Agency.
dc-wic: WIC gives healthy food, breastfeeding support, nutrition education, and health referrals to pregnant and postpartum people, infants, and children up to age 5. DC Health runs it through local WIC clinics. To start, call your local WIC site, or reach the DC WIC team at (202) 442-9397. You can find site locations at dcwic.org/wic-locations.
new-mexico-child-tax-credit: New Mexico has a refundable Child Tax Credit worth up to $637 per qualifying child for the lowest-income families, with the amount stepping down as income rises. Because it is refundable, it can come back as cash even if you owe no tax. There is no separate application: you claim it on your New Mexico personal income tax return, Form PIT-1, for each qualifying child.
colorado-snap-food-assistance: SNAP is Colorado's food assistance program: monthly food money loaded onto a Colorado Quest EBT card you use like a debit card at most grocery stores. Apply online through Colorado PEAK at colorado.gov/PEAK, which also handles Health First Colorado, Colorado Works cash, and other benefits, or at your county human services office. The state SNAP customer service line at 1-800-816-4451 answers questions about an existing case.
michigan-medicaid-and-healthy-michigan-p: Michigan Medicaid is free or low-cost health coverage for children, pregnant people, parents, older adults, people with disabilities, and low-income adults. The Healthy Michigan Plan covers adults 19 to 64 who meet the income rules. Apply online through MI Bridges at newmibridges.michigan.gov, by phone at 1-855-789-5610, or at your local MDHHS office.
kansas-lieap-low-income-energy-assistanc: LIEAP is Kansas's Low Income Energy Assistance Program: a once-a-year benefit that helps pay winter heating costs, run by the Department for Children and Families. The application period is a set winter window that has closed for 2026, and DCF posts the next window when it is set. Apply through the DCF Self-Service Portal at cssp.kees.ks.gov during the window, or at a local DCF service center. Questions: Benefits Assistance at 1-888-369-4777.
kansas-tanf-cash-assistance-successful-f: Kansas calls its TANF cash assistance the Successful Families Program: monthly cash for low-income families with children, paid on the Kansas Benefits Card, paired with work activities. Strict time limits apply. Apply through the DCF Self-Service Portal at cssp.kees.ks.gov or at your local DCF service center. For help, call Benefits Assistance at 1-888-369-4777 or DCF Customer Service at 1-833-765-2003.
new-mexico-legal-aid: New Mexico Legal Aid gives free civil legal help to low-income residents on the noncriminal problems that upend a household: eviction and housing, family matters, public benefits, consumer and debt issues, and more. Call the statewide intake line at 1-833-545-4357 (1-833-LGL-HELP) or apply online. Free plain-language legal information for everyone is at LawHelpNewMexico.com.
ohio-legal-help-eviction-and-legal-aid: Free, plain-language legal information for Ohioans, guided court-form tools through a MyOLH account, and a Find a Lawyer directory to reach local legal aid. Ohio Legal Help covers eviction, housing, debt, family law, and public benefits.
liheap-energy-assistance-illinois: Illinois LIHEAP helps low-income households pay heating and cooling bills, with priority help for emergencies. Apply during your assignment month at helpillinoisfamilies.com or through a local Community Action Agency; the Help Illinois Families hotline is 1-833-711-0374. For the 2025-2026 program year, applications run from fall 2025 through August 15, 2026, or until funding runs out.
arizona-liheap-and-power-az-utility-assi: LIHEAP helps low-income Arizona households pay home energy bills, run by DES through local Community Action Agencies. Standard help is up to $640 toward your utility bill, and a household facing a shutoff can qualify for an added one-time crisis payment of up to $500 per 12-month period. Apply through the DES online portal, or contact your local Community Action Agency, which takes applications and can help you complete them.
delaware-healthy-children-program-chip: The Delaware Healthy Children Program is the state's CHIP coverage for uninsured children under age 19 whose family earns a little too much for Medicaid. As of July 1, 2024, there are no monthly premiums, and there are no copays for medical care or prescriptions except for non-emergency use of the emergency room. Apply through Delaware ASSIST at assist.dhss.delaware.gov, or call 1-800-996-9969 to request an application.
indiana-earned-income-credit: Indiana has its own Earned Income Credit worth 10 percent of your federal Earned Income Tax Credit, and it is refundable, so it can come back as cash even if you owe no state tax. You claim it by filing an Indiana income tax return and attaching Schedule IN-EIC. You generally must qualify for the federal credit first.
legal-services-of-north-dakota: Legal Services of North Dakota provides free civil legal help to low-income and older North Dakotans on housing, family, public benefits, consumer, and veteran matters. Call the statewide intake line at 1-800-634-5263, or if you are age 60 or older call the senior line at 1-866-621-9886. Intake runs Monday through Thursday, 9am to 3pm Central.
care-4-kids-child-care-assistance: Care 4 Kids helps low-to-moderate-income Connecticut families pay for child care, so a parent can work, train, or attend school. Run by the Office of Early Childhood, it pays part of the cost directly to an approved provider. Apply online through the Care 4 Kids portal, or call 1-888-214-5437 with questions.
soonercare-oklahoma-medicaid: SoonerCare is Oklahoma's Medicaid program: free or low-cost health coverage for children, pregnant people, parents, older adults, people with disabilities, and low-income adults. Oklahoma expanded SoonerCare in 2021 to cover adults ages 19 to 64. Apply online at mysoonercare.org, or call the SoonerCare Helpline at 1-800-987-7767.
indiana-wic: WIC gives healthy food, breastfeeding support, nutrition education, and health referrals to pregnant and postpartum people, infants, and children up to age 5. Indiana WIC runs through the Indiana Department of Health and local clinics. Find your local clinic through the INWIC app or at in.gov/health/wic, or call 1-800-522-0874 for more information.
clinica-sierra-vista: Community health centers across Kern County offering medical, dental, and behavioral health care whether or not you have insurance. Staff can also help you sign up for Medi-Cal or Covered California.
unemployment-insurance-kentucky: Temporary weekly payments if you lost work through no fault of your own, from the Kentucky Office of Unemployment Insurance. File your claim online at kcc.ky.gov, which is the fastest way, or by phone at 502-564-2900 using the automated system. Make sure you are on a .ky.gov website when you file, and only trust unemployment emails from an @ky.gov address.
indiana-tanf-cash-assistance: Temporary Assistance for Needy Families, TANF, is Indiana's monthly cash assistance for low-income families with a child under 18. Most adults take part in IMPACT, the state's employment and training program, which includes an Applicant Job Search step before benefits start. Apply online through the FSSA Benefits Portal at fssabenefits.in.gov or at your local DFR office. Call 1-800-403-0864 for help.
lieap-low-income-energy-assistance-progr: LIEAP helps low-income West Virginia households pay winter heating costs, either as a payment to your utility company or a direct payment. An Emergency LIEAP component helps households without resources facing the loss of a heating source. Apply online through wvPATH at wvpath.wv.gov, at your local Department of Human Services field office, or through a local Community Action agency or Area Agency on Aging.
indiana-snap-food-assistance: SNAP is Indiana's food assistance program: monthly food money on a Hoosier Works EBT card you use like a debit card at most grocery stores. The Division of Family Resources runs it. Apply online through the FSSA Benefits Portal at fssabenefits.in.gov, which also handles Medicaid and TANF cash on one application, or at your local DFR office. You can also call 1-800-403-0864, Monday through Friday, 8am to 4:30pm local time.
new-hampshire-snap-food-assistance: SNAP is New Hampshire's food assistance program: monthly food money on an EBT card you use like a debit card at most grocery stores. Apply online through NH EASY at nheasy.nh.gov, the state's system that also covers cash assistance, Medicaid, and child care on one application, or at your local DHHS District Office. You can also call the DHHS Customer Service Center at 1-844-275-3447 to have an application mailed to you.
capk-wic-women-infants-and-children: Free healthy food, nutrition help, and breastfeeding support for pregnant women, new moms, and kids under 5. Dads, grandparents, and foster parents caring for young children can also apply.
weatherization-assistance-program-maine: Free home energy-efficiency work for income-eligible Maine households: a home energy assessment first, then air sealing, insulation, and heating-system improvements that lower future bills. Community Action Agencies deliver the program across Maine. Homeowners, renters, and owners of small 2- to 4-unit buildings can qualify. Contact your local Community Action Agency to apply, since applying for HEAP also puts you in line for weatherization.
211-iowa: Dial 2-1-1 from any Iowa phone, or call 1-800-244-7431, for free, confidential help finding local assistance with housing, utilities, food, healthcare, and more. 211 Iowa connects you to thousands of local programs and answers every day. You can also text your zip code to 898211 or search at 211iowa.org.
weatherization-assistance-program-massac: Free home energy-efficiency work for income-eligible Massachusetts households: insulation, air sealing, and heating-system improvements that lower future bills. Your Fuel Assistance application also serves as your weatherization application, so households eligible for Home Energy Assistance are eligible for weatherization. Contact your local agency, or call the Cold Relief Heatline at 1-800-632-8175.
louisiana-snap-food-assistance: SNAP is Louisiana's food assistance program: monthly food money loaded onto a Louisiana Purchase EBT card you use like a debit card at most grocery stores. SNAP is now run by the Louisiana Department of Health's Office of Economic Stability, but you apply the same way as always: online through the CAFE Self-Service Portal, or by phone at 1-888-524-3578 (1-888-LA-HELP-U). You can also text GETSNAP to 898211 for information.
lawhelpny-org-eviction-and-legal-help: Free, plain-language legal information for New Yorkers and a directory of local legal aid, covering eviction, debt, public benefits, family law, and more. Search by your county or zip code to find the programs and hotlines that serve your area.
home-energy-assistance-program-heap-lihe: HEAP is Maine's LIHEAP heating help for income-eligible homeowners and renters, covering fuel costs, emergency fuel delivery, and some energy-related repairs and utility payments. Local Community Action Agencies handle applications, not MaineHousing directly. Apply online, or find your local agency by zip code. The 2026-2027 season opened August 3, 2026 and runs until funds run out or May 29, 2027. For more information call 1-877-544-3271.
mississippi-snap-food-assistance: SNAP is Mississippi's food assistance program: monthly food money on an EBT card you use like a debit card at most grocery stores. Apply online through the Access MS Common Web Portal at access.ms.gov, or at your local MDHS county office. Questions about a SNAP or TANF case go to the MDHS EAE Client Services line at 1-800-948-3050.
mississippi-tanf-cash-assistance: Temporary Assistance for Needy Families, TANF, is Mississippi's monthly cash assistance for low-income families with children. Most adults take part in the TANF Work Program, which helps you build job skills and find work. Apply online through the Access MS portal at access.ms.gov or at your local MDHS county office. A 60-month lifetime limit applies.
kentucky-child-care-assistance-program-c: The Child Care Assistance Program, CCAP, helps low-income Kentucky families pay for child care while parents work, train, or go to school. Apply online through kynect at kynect.ky.gov or by phone at 1-855-306-8959. A prescreening tool on kynect can tell you if you likely qualify before you apply.
unemployment-insurance-maine-department-: Temporary weekly payments if you lost work through no fault of your own, from the Maine Department of Labor. File online through ReEmployME, which is the fastest way, or call the claim center at 1-800-593-7660, Monday through Friday, 8am to 3pm. TTY users dial Maine Relay 711.
legal-aid-services-of-oklahoma: Legal Aid Services of Oklahoma provides free civil legal help to low-income residents on housing, family, public benefits, consumer, and other noncriminal matters. Call the statewide line at 1-888-534-5243 to reach the office serving your area, or find free legal information and self-help tools at oklaw.org.
211info-oregon-211: Dial 2-1-1 from any Oregon phone for free, confidential help finding local assistance with housing, utilities, food, healthcare, and more. 211info is a statewide service. You can also text your zip code to 898211 to get connected to local resources, or search at 211info.org.
weatherization-assistance-program-missou: Free home energy-efficiency work for income-eligible Missouri households: insulation, air sealing, and heating-system improvements that lower future bills. The Missouri Department of Natural Resources runs the program through a statewide network of local weatherization agencies. Contact the local agency serving your area to apply, since DNR does not take applications directly.
nebraska-adc-aid-to-dependent-children-t: Aid to Dependent Children, ADC, is Nebraska's TANF cash assistance for low-income families with children. Most working-age adults take part in Employment First, which helps you move toward a job through training and work preparation. Apply online through iServe Nebraska at iserve.nebraska.gov or at your local DHHS office.
unemployment-insurance-maryland: Temporary weekly payments if you lost work through no fault of your own, from the Maryland Department of Labor. File online through the BEACON system at beacon.labor.maryland.gov, which is the fastest way, or call a claims agent at 667-207-6520, Monday through Friday, 8am to 4pm. You must certify each week to keep payments coming.
weatherization-assistance-program-nys-hc: Free home energy-efficiency work for income-eligible New Yorkers: insulation, air sealing, and health-and-safety fixes that lower future bills, at no cost to those who qualify. Run by NYS Homes and Community Renewal through local agencies in all 62 counties, and combined with the EmPower+ application.
alaska-medicaid-and-denali-kidcare: Alaska Medicaid is free or low-cost health coverage for children, pregnant people, families, seniors, people with disabilities, and low-income adults. Alaska expanded Medicaid in 2015 to cover adults ages 19 to 64 without dependent children, and Denali KidCare covers children and pregnant people. Apply through HealthCare.gov or the Alaska Connect portal, or call the Virtual Contact Center at 800-478-7778.
weatherization-assistance-program-wyomin: Wyoming's Weatherization Assistance Program makes free energy-efficiency improvements that lower future heating bills: insulation, air sealing, and heating-system repairs. It shares one application with LIEAP, and the Utility Assistance portal takes weatherization applications year-round. Call 1-800-246-4221 for help. Homeowners and renters both qualify, including people in mobile homes.
liheap-energy-assistance-louisiana: LIHEAP helps low-income Louisiana households pay home energy bills, through the Louisiana Housing Corporation and local Community Action Agencies. It covers heating help in winter, cooling help in summer, and year-round crisis help when your power is shut off or about to be. Apply online through LHC or through the local agency serving your parish.
georgialegalaid-org-eviction-and-legal-h: Free plain-language legal information for Georgians on eviction, foreclosure, public benefits, family law, and debt, run by Atlanta Legal Aid and the Georgia Legal Services Program, with self-help forms and a virtual assistant.
weatherization-assistance-program-kansas: Free home energy-efficiency work for income-eligible Kansas households: air sealing, insulation, and heating and cooling repairs that lower future bills. Kansas Housing Resources Corporation runs the program through local provider agencies. Contact KHRC at 785-217-2001 to be connected to the provider serving your county, since KHRC does not weatherize homes directly.
liheap-energy-bill-assistance: Federal program that helps pay heating and cooling bills, and can help in a shutoff emergency. Run by state and local agencies.
connecticut-legal-aid-statewide-legal-se: Connecticut's legal aid programs give free civil legal help to low-income residents on housing, family, public benefits, consumer, and other noncriminal matters. Call Statewide Legal Services of Connecticut at 1-800-453-3320 to reach the legal aid program serving your area, or apply online any time at apply.slsct.org. Free self-help legal information is at ctlawhelp.org.
va-benefits-veterans: Disability compensation, pensions, healthcare, housing help, and more for veterans and eligible family members.
legal-aid-of-nebraska: Legal Aid of Nebraska provides free civil legal help to low-income residents on housing and eviction, family, public benefits, consumer, and debt matters. Call the AccessLine at 1-877-250-2016 to apply. Nebraskans 60 and older can use the ElderAccessLine at 1-800-527-7249, and a disaster line runs at 1-844-268-5627. Find more at legalaidofnebraska.org.
unemployment-benefits-north-carolina: Temporary weekly payments if you lost work through no fault of your own, from the NC Division of Employment Security. File online through MyNCUIBenefits at des.nc.gov, which is the fastest way. For help, call the UI Support Center at 888-737-0259.
raft-residential-assistance-for-families: RAFT is Massachusetts's active emergency housing assistance: up to $7,000 per household in a 12-month period to help with overdue rent, mortgage payments, utility bills, and moving costs when you face eviction, foreclosure, or loss of utilities. Apply online at ApplyHousingHelp.Mass.Gov, where your application is handled by a Regional Administering Agency. Both a tenant and a landlord application are needed for rental help.
2-1-1-arizona: Dial 2-1-1 from any Arizona phone, or call 1-877-211-8661 from anywhere in the state, for free, confidential help finding local assistance with housing, utilities, food, health, and more. 2-1-1 Arizona, a program of Solari, answers from 9am to 7pm, seven days a week, in English and Spanish. You can also search at 211arizona.org.
utah-earned-income-tax-credit: Utah offers a state Earned Income Tax Credit worth 20 percent of your federal EITC. It is nonrefundable, which means it lowers the Utah income tax you owe but does not pay out as a refund on its own, and you cannot carry any unused part to another year. Claim it on your Utah income tax return if you qualified for the federal EITC.
nebraska-earned-income-tax-credit: Nebraska has a refundable Earned Income Tax Credit worth 10 percent of your federal EITC. Because it is refundable, it can come back to you as cash even when you owe no state income tax. Claim it on your Nebraska individual income tax return, Form 1040N, after you claim the federal credit.
weatherization-assistance-program-montan: Free home energy-efficiency work for income-eligible Montana households: insulation, air sealing, and heating-system repairs that lower future bills. Both homeowners and renters can apply, at any time of year, using the combined LIEAP and Weatherization application filed with your local eligibility office. For help, call the Human and Community Services Division at 406-444-1788.
kern-county-veterans-service-department: Free help for veterans and their families filing VA claims: disability compensation, pensions, health care, education, and survivor benefits. Accredited officers handle the paperwork with you at no charge.
virginia-energy-assistance-program-fuel-: The Energy Assistance Program helps low-income Virginia households with home energy costs through three seasonal parts: Fuel Assistance for heating, Crisis Assistance for a heating emergency, and Cooling Assistance for summer. Apply online through CommonHelp, at your local department of social services, or by phone at 1-855-635-4370, Monday through Friday, 7am to 6pm.
badgercare-plus-wisconsin-medicaid: BadgerCare Plus is Wisconsin's largest Medicaid program: free or low-cost health coverage for children, pregnant people, parents, and other adults with low income, ages 0 to 64. It covers preventive care, doctor visits, prescriptions, and emergencies. Apply online through ACCESS at access.wisconsin.gov, or through your local county or tribal agency. Call ForwardHealth Member Services at 1-800-362-3002, Monday through Friday, 8am to 6pm.
weatherization-assistance-program-gefa: Free whole-house energy efficiency improvements for income-qualified Georgia households: air and duct sealing, insulation, and HVAC upgrades that shrink future bills. The Georgia Environmental Finance Authority runs it through local community action agencies.
nj-familycare-medicaid-and-chip: NJ FamilyCare is New Jersey's publicly funded health coverage, covering Medicaid and CHIP. It pays for doctor visits, prescriptions, vision, dental, mental health and substance use care, and hospital stays for qualified residents of any age. Apply online or call the hotline at 1-800-701-0710. Children under 19 can apply regardless of immigration status.
north-dakota-medicaid-expanded: North Dakota Medicaid is free or low-cost health coverage for children, pregnant people, parents, older adults, people with disabilities, and low-income adults. The state expanded Medicaid, so low-income adults ages 19 to 64 can qualify. Apply online through the Self Service Portal at applyforhelp.nd.gov, or by phone through the HHS Customer Support Center at 1-866-614-6005.
new-york-wic: Healthy food on an eWIC card, nutrition counseling, and breastfeeding support for pregnant and postpartum people, infants, and children under 5. Apply through your local WIC office; chat with Wanda, the online WIC assistant, or call the NYS WIC Program at 518-402-7093 to get connected.
chip-childrens-health-insurance-program: Pennsylvania CHIP covers uninsured children and teens up to age 19 who are not eligible for Medical Assistance, with no family income limit that blocks enrollment. For most families CHIP is free; others pay low monthly premiums. Apply online or call the CHIP helpline at 1-800-986-5437.
reemployment-assistance-south-dakota-une: Reemployment Assistance is South Dakota's unemployment program: temporary weekly payments if you lost your job through no fault of your own, run by the Department of Labor and Regulation. File your claim online at sd.gov/rabenefits, which is the fastest way, or call the Reemployment Assistance line at 605-626-2452 for help.
maryland-energy-assistance-office-of-hom: The Office of Home Energy Programs, OHEP, helps low-income Maryland households with home energy costs. It runs the Maryland Energy Assistance Program (MEAP) for heating grants, the Electric Universal Service Program (EUSP) for electric bills, and arrearage retirement help for past-due balances. Apply online through MarylandBenefits at MarylandBenefits.gov, at your local home energy program office, or by phone at 1-800-332-6347.
child-care-services-twc-scholarships: Child care scholarships that pay most of the cost of care for low-income working Texas families, run by the Texas Workforce Commission through local Workforce Solutions offices. Apply through childcare.texas.gov.
kentucky-k-tap-cash-assistance: K-TAP, the Kentucky Transitional Assistance Program, is the state's monthly cash assistance for low-income families with children. It is Kentucky's version of TANF, and most adults take part in the Kentucky Works program, which helps you move toward a job. Apply online through kynect at kynect.ky.gov, by phone at 1-855-306-8959, or at your local DCBS office.
hawki-healthy-and-well-kids-in-iowa: Hawki, short for Healthy and Well Kids in Iowa, is low-cost health and dental coverage for children under 19 in working families who earn too much for Medicaid. Most families pay nothing, and no family pays more than $40 a month for all of its children combined. Apply online through the HHS Services Portal at hhsservices.iowa.gov, or call Hawki Member Services at 1-800-257-8563.
food-and-nutrition-services-north-caroli: Food and Nutrition Services is North Carolina's name for SNAP, monthly food money on an EBT card you use like a debit card at the grocery store. Apply online at epass.nc.gov, in person at your county Department of Social Services, or by mailing a paper application to your county DSS.
alaska-temporary-assistance-program-cash: The Alaska Temporary Assistance Program, ATAP, is the state's TANF program: monthly cash assistance and work services for low-income families with children. Most adults follow a Work First plan of job search, training, or work experience while the cash steadies the household. Apply online through the Alaska Connect portal or by phone through the Virtual Contact Center at 800-478-7778.
low-income-energy-assistance-program-nor: LIEAP is a one-time yearly payment sent to your heating vendor to help with winter heating costs. The application window is set: households with someone 60 or older or a disabled person getting services through the Division of Aging and Adult Services can apply December 1-31, and all other households apply January 1 through March 31 or until funds run out. Apply at your county Department of Social Services or online at epass.nc.gov.
211-utah: Dial 2-1-1 from any Utah phone, or call 1-888-826-9790, for free, confidential help finding local assistance with housing, utilities, food, healthcare, and more. 211 Utah answers by phone seven days a week, 8am to 6pm. You can also text your zip code to 801-845-2211 on weekdays or search at 211utah.org.
delaware-energy-assistance-program-lihea: The Delaware Energy Assistance Program helps low-income households with home energy costs in three parts: winter heating assistance from October 1 through March 31, year-round crisis assistance for a shutoff or empty fuel tank, and summer cooling assistance that can include a free window air conditioner. Community partners run intake. Apply through Delaware ASSIST at assist.dhss.delaware.gov, call the Division of Social Services at 302-255-9875, or call Catholic Charities in your county.
twc-unemployment-benefits: Temporary, partial income replacement if you lost your job or had hours cut through no fault of your own. Apply online through Unemployment Benefit Services or by phone at the TWC Tele-Center.
north-dakota-liheap-energy-assistance: The Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program, LIHEAP, helps income-eligible North Dakota households with home heating and energy costs, and it can also help in a heating emergency. Apply online through the Self Service Portal at applyforhelp.nd.gov, or by phone through the HHS Customer Support Center at 1-866-614-6005. Ask about the current application dates when you call, since the heating-season window matters.
south-dakota-child-care-assistance: The Child Care Assistance program helps low-income working families in South Dakota pay for child care. You qualify by meeting income guidelines and a minimum work or school requirement, and you may owe a small co-payment based on your income and family size. Apply through your local Department of Social Services office. Call 1-800-227-3020 for help.
medicaid-ohio: Ohio Medicaid is free or low-cost health coverage for children, pregnant people, adults, older adults, and people with disabilities. Adults 19 to 64 can qualify with income at or below 138 percent of the federal poverty level under the Group VIII adult category. Apply online through Ohio Benefits at benefits.ohio.gov or by phone at 1-844-640-6446.
snap-food-stamps-pennsylvania: Pennsylvania SNAP loads monthly food money on an EBT ACCESS card. Apply online at COMPASS (compass.dhs.pa.gov), at your county assistance office, or by mail. The DHS Helpline is 1-800-692-7462.
south-dakota-tanf-cash-assistance: Temporary Assistance for Needy Families, TANF, is South Dakota's monthly cash assistance for low-income families with children. Most adults must take part in work activities, generally 30 hours a week, or 20 hours if you care for a child under 6. Apply online at eaportal.sd.gov or at your local Department of Social Services office. Call 605-773-3165 with questions.
unemployment-insurance-new-hampshire: Temporary weekly payments if you lost work through no fault of your own, from New Hampshire Employment Security. File online at nhes.nh.gov, which is the fastest way. If you need help, the NHES claims line is 603-271-7700, open Monday through Friday, 8am to 4:30pm.
medical-assistance-pennsylvania-medicaid: Medical Assistance is Pennsylvania's Medicaid: free or low-cost health coverage delivered through HealthChoices managed care plans. Adults 19 to 64 can qualify with income at or below 133 percent of the federal poverty guidelines. Apply at COMPASS, your county assistance office, or by phone at 1-866-550-4355.
new-hampshire-medicaid-and-granite-advan: New Hampshire Medicaid is free or low-cost health coverage for children, pregnant people, parents, seniors, people with disabilities, and low-income adults. The Granite Advantage Health Care Program is the part that covers low-income adults age 19 through 64. Apply online through NH EASY at nheasy.nh.gov, or call the DHHS Customer Service Center at 1-844-275-3447, Monday through Friday, 8am to 4pm.
211-connects-alabama: Dial 2-1-1 from any Alabama phone, or call 1-888-421-1266, for free, confidential help finding local assistance with housing, utilities, food, healthcare, and more. 211 Connects Alabama answers 24 hours a day, every day of the year. You can also text your zip code, or the keyword 211KNOW, to 898211.
south-dakota-snap-food-assistance: SNAP is South Dakota's food assistance program: monthly food money on an EBT card you use like a debit card at most grocery stores. Apply online through the DSS Benefits Portal at eaportal.sd.gov, at your local Department of Social Services office, or with a paper application you mail or drop off. For help, call the Department of Social Services at 605-773-3165.
weatherization-assistance-program-louisi: Free home energy-efficiency work for income-eligible Louisiana households: insulation, air sealing, and heating and cooling repairs that lower future bills. The Louisiana Housing Corporation runs the Weatherization Assistance Program through regional providers. Contact the provider serving your area to apply, since LHC does not take applications directly. Both homeowners and renters can qualify.
greater-bakersfield-legal-assistance-gbl: Free legal help for low-income Kern County residents: eviction defense, denied or cut-off benefits (CalWORKs, CalFresh, SSI), restraining orders for domestic violence survivors, health coverage problems, and a Seniors Law Center for people 60 and older.
kern-medical: Kern County's public teaching hospital in Bakersfield, home to the region's only Level II trauma center. Covered California counselors are on site weekdays to help patients get insured.
m-street-navigation-center-capk: A 24-hour shelter in Bakersfield with beds, meals, laundry, medical check-ups, and secure storage. Pets welcome. Staff help connect guests to longer-term housing.
kentucky-liheap-home-energy-assistance: LIHEAP helps low-income Kentucky households with home heating and cooling costs. It runs through Community Action Kentucky's network of local Community Action Agencies, which cover all 120 counties, not through a single state office. Contact the Community Action Agency serving your county to apply, or call 1-800-456-3452 to find your local office. Applications open in set seasonal windows.
arkansas-liheap-energy-assistance: The Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program, LIHEAP, helps Arkansas households pay heating and cooling bills, with extra crisis help when your power or heat is about to be shut off. Applications are taken by local community action agencies, not by a state office. Find the agency serving your county through the Arkansas Community Action Agencies Association at acaaa.org, or call 501-372-0807.
west-virginia-wic: WIC gives healthy food, breastfeeding support, nutrition education, and health referrals to pregnant and postpartum people, infants, and children up to age 5. West Virginia WIC runs through local clinics tied to county health departments. Check the WIC eligibility screening tool and find your nearest clinic through the state WIC clinic search, then call the clinic to book your first appointment.
aged-blind-or-disabled-abd-cash-assistan: ABD is a Washington cash program from DSHS for low-income adults who are 65 or older, blind, or likely to meet the Social Security disability standard. It pays a monthly cash grant while helping you apply for federal SSI, and it can connect you to the Housing and Essential Needs (HEN) program. Apply at washingtonconnection.org or by phone at 1-877-501-2233.
liheap-home-energy-assistance: Florida's LIHEAP helps income-qualified households pay home cooling and heating bills, including year-round crisis help when service is about to be shut off. FloridaCommerce funds local agencies across the state that take applications.
general-assistance-maine: General Assistance is Maine's municipal safety-net program that helps people meet immediate basic needs when they cannot afford them, including rent, mortgage, room rent, temporary housing, heating fuel, food, and household supplies. Apply in person at your local town or city office, and help is paid as a voucher directly to the vendor. If you cannot reach your local office, call the state hotline at 1-800-442-6003.
hawaii-home-energy-assistance-program-h-: The Hawaii Home Energy Assistance Program (H-HEAP), formerly LIHEAP, gives income-eligible households a one-time payment toward an electric or gas bill for heating or cooling. It has two parts: Energy Crisis Intervention (ECI) for households with a utility disconnect notice, accepted year-round with a limited number of approvals each month, and Energy Credit (EC) for bill help without a crisis, accepted only June 1 through June 30 each year. Applications are processed only by the Community Action Agency serving your island, not by DHS offices.
maine-tanf-cash-assistance: Temporary Assistance for Needy Families, TANF, is Maine's monthly cash assistance for low-income families with children and pregnant people. Most adults take part in the ASPIRE work program, which helps you move toward a job. Apply online through My Maine Connection at mymaineconnection.gov, or call the Office for Family Independence at 1-855-797-4357, Monday through Friday, 7am to 4pm, and choose the TANF option.
sc-211: Dial 2-1-1 from any South Carolina phone, or call 1-866-892-9211, for free, confidential help finding local assistance with housing, utilities, food, healthcare, and more. SC 211 is operated by the United Way Association of South Carolina and answers around the clock, every day. You can also text HELP or AYUDA to 211-211, or search at sc211.org.
new-hampshire-fuel-assistance-program-li: The Fuel Assistance Program helps income-eligible New Hampshire households pay winter heating costs. The New Hampshire Department of Energy runs it through the state's Community Action Agencies, which take the applications and pay your heating vendor directly. Contact the Community Action Agency serving your area to apply, or dial 2-1-1 to find it.
health-first-colorado-medicaid-and-chp: Health First Colorado is the state's Medicaid program: free or low-cost health coverage for children, pregnant people, parents, adults, older adults, and people with disabilities. Child Health Plan Plus, CHP+, covers children and pregnant people at slightly higher incomes. Apply online through Colorado PEAK at colorado.gov/PEAK or at your county human services office. The Member Contact Center is 1-800-221-3943, Monday through Friday, 8am to 4:30pm.
weatherization-assistance-program-nevada: Free home energy-efficiency work for income-eligible Nevada households: air sealing, insulation, and heating and cooling improvements that lower future bills. The Nevada Housing Division runs the program through local nonprofit agencies. Both homeowners and renters qualify, though the owner of a rental may have to cover part of the cost. Contact the agency serving your county to apply.
missingmoney-unclaimed-property-search: Official state-endorsed search for money owed to you: old deposits, uncashed checks, forgotten accounts. Free — never pay anyone to claim it.
rhode-island-legal-services: Rhode Island Legal Services provides free civil legal help to low-income residents on housing and eviction, family, public benefits, consumer, and elder law matters. Call the office at 401-274-2652, or the toll-free line at 1-800-662-5034, to reach intake, or apply for help online. This is civil legal help only, not criminal defense.
new-york-medicaid: Free or low-cost health coverage for low-income New Yorkers. Adults 19 to 64 can qualify with income up to 138 percent of the federal poverty level, about $1,836 a month for one person in 2026. Apply through NY State of Health, the state's official marketplace, or call the Medicaid Helpline at 1-800-541-2831.
mississippi-wic: WIC gives healthy food, breastfeeding support, nutrition education, and health referrals to pregnant, breastfeeding, and postpartum women, infants, and children under age 5. Mississippi WIC runs through county health department clinics of the Mississippi State Department of Health. Call 1-800-545-6747, or 601-991-6000 in the Jackson area, to find your local clinic and start.
weatherization-assistance-program-minnes: Free home energy-efficiency work for income-qualified Minnesota households: insulation, air sealing, and heating-system repairs that permanently lower your energy bills. Both homeowners and renters can qualify. The Department of Commerce runs the program through local service providers, and it shares one joint application with Energy Assistance. Call the Commerce Energy Information Center at 1-800-657-3710 to reach the provider serving your area.
unemployment-benefits-michigan: Temporary weekly payments if you lost work through no fault of your own, from the Michigan Unemployment Insurance Agency. File online through MiWAM at michigan.gov/uia, which is the fastest way, or by phone at 1-866-500-0017. The customer service line is open Monday through Friday, 8am to 4:30pm.
kansas-child-care-assistance: Child Care Assistance pays part of the cost of child care so parents can work, look for work, or attend school, with the benefit loaded onto the Kansas Benefits Card and paid to DCF-enrolled providers. Apply through the DCF Self-Service Portal at cssp.kees.ks.gov, or call Benefits Assistance at 1-888-369-4777. Processing can take up to 30 days.
kern-behavioral-health-24-hour-crisis-ho: Free, confidential 24-hour support for mental health or substance use crises, or just to talk to a trained counselor without judgment. They can also send a Mobile Crisis Response team and connect you to ongoing care.
california-liheap-energy-assistance: Help paying energy bills and shutoff emergencies, delivered through local community action agencies.
kentucky-medicaid-and-kchip: Kentucky Medicaid is free or low-cost health coverage for children, pregnant people, parents, older adults, people with disabilities, and low-income adults. Kentucky expanded Medicaid in 2014 to cover adults ages 19 to 64 with income up to 138 percent of the federal poverty level, and KCHIP covers children through CHIP. Apply online through kynect at kynect.ky.gov/benefits, or call kynect at 1-855-459-6328.
unemployment-insurance-indiana-dwd-uplin: Temporary weekly payments if you lost work through no fault of your own, from the Indiana Department of Workforce Development. File your claim online through Uplink, the Claimant Self Service system, at uplink.in.gov, which is the fastest way. For help, call 1-800-891-6499. You must file a weekly voucher for each week to be paid.
unemployment-insurance-edd: Weekly payments of $40 to $450 if you lost work through no fault of your own. Apply online through myEDD; first payment usually takes about three weeks.
nc-medicaid: NC Medicaid is free or low-cost health coverage for children, pregnant people, parents, older adults, people with disabilities, and low-income adults. Since December 2023, adults 19 to 64 can qualify with income up to 138 percent of the federal poverty level. Apply at epass.nc.gov, at HealthCare.gov, or at your county Department of Social Services.
crisis-intervention-program-cip-stokes-c: CIP helps if you are in a heating or cooling emergency, like a shut-off notice in winter or summer. It can pay up to $600 per crisis, sent straight to your utility company. You can get help more than once, up to $600 total per state fiscal year.
dc-energy-assistance-liheap-and-utility-: The Department of Energy and Environment, DOEE, runs the District's home energy help. As of the last check, DOEE has stopped taking new LIHEAP applications and is directing residents to the Utility Discount Program, UDP. The regular LIHEAP benefit ranges from $200 to $1,800 based on household size, income, heating source, and dwelling type, with a separate crisis benefit for households facing disconnection. Call 311 or (202) 737-4404 to check an application status or ask what help is open right now.
mississippi-medicaid-and-chip: Mississippi Medicaid is free or low-cost health coverage for children, pregnant people, parents and caretakers of minor children, older adults, and people with disabilities, and CHIP covers children in families that earn a bit more. Mississippi has not expanded Medicaid, so most low-income adults without children or a disability do not qualify. Check eligibility and apply at medicaid.ms.gov, or call 1-800-421-2408.
ceap-comprehensive-energy-assistance-pro: Texas's LIHEAP utility assistance: helps low-income households pay electric, gas, and propane bills, including in a shutoff crisis. Local agencies in all 254 counties take applications; find yours through TDHCA's Help for Texans page.
wisconsin-earned-income-credit: Wisconsin's Earned Income Credit is a refundable credit for working families with at least one qualifying child, worth a percentage of your federal EITC: 4 percent with one child, 11 percent with two children, and 34 percent with three or more children. It is refundable, so it can pay out even if you owe no state tax. Claim it on your Wisconsin income tax return (Form 1 or 1NPR).
west-virginia-medicaid: West Virginia Medicaid is free or low-cost health coverage for children, pregnant people, parents, older adults, people with disabilities, and low-income adults. West Virginia expanded Medicaid, so adults 19 to 64 with low income can qualify on their own. Apply online through wvPATH at wvpath.wv.gov, at a local Department of Human Services field office, or by calling the DoHS Customer Service Center at 1-877-716-1212.
montana-medicaid-and-healthy-montana-kid: Montana Medicaid and Healthy Montana Kids (HMK) Plus are free or low-cost health coverage for children, pregnant people, parents, older adults, people with disabilities, and low-income adults. Montana expanded Medicaid, so adults ages 19 to 64 with low income may qualify through the HELP Plan. Apply online at apply.mt.gov or at your local Office of Public Assistance at 1-888-706-1535. For questions about current benefits, call the Member Help Line at 1-800-362-8312, Monday through Friday, 8am to 5pm.
washington-working-families-tax-credit: The Working Families Tax Credit is Washington's refundable cash credit, run by the Department of Revenue. For the 2025 credit it pays up to $335 with no qualifying children, $660 with one child, $995 with two, and $1,330 with three or more, with a $50 minimum for those who qualify. Apply for free at workingfamiliescredit.wa.gov after you file your federal return.
new-hampshire-wic: WIC gives healthy food, breastfeeding support, nutrition education, and health referrals to pregnant and postpartum people, infants, and children up to age 5. New Hampshire WIC runs through local clinics statewide. To apply, find your nearest clinic at signupwic.com, or call the State WIC Agency at 1-800-942-4321.
oklahoma-liheap-energy-assistance: The Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program, LIHEAP, helps low-income Oklahoma households with home energy costs in three seasonal parts: Winter Heating, the Energy Crisis Assistance Program for a heating or cooling emergency, and Summer Cooling. Apply online at OKDHSLive.org during each open enrollment window. For a life-threatening energy crisis, call 405-522-5050 year-round.
aloha-united-way-211-hawaii: Dial 2-1-1 anywhere in Hawaii to reach the Aloha United Way 211 helpline, a free and confidential service that connects you to local help with food, rent, utilities, healthcare, and more, drawn from a database of over 1,400 agencies and 4,000 programs. Specialists answer from 7am to 10pm, seven days a week. From outside Hawaii, or to text, use 1-877-275-6569, and you can search anytime at search.auw211.org.
alabama-snap-food-assistance: SNAP is Alabama's food assistance program: monthly food money on an EBT card you use like a debit card at most grocery stores. Apply online through MyDHR at mydhr.alabama.gov, run by the Alabama Department of Human Resources, or at your county DHR office. Older adults with no earned income can use a shorter application through the Alabama Elderly Simplified Application Project.
floridalawhelp-org-eviction-and-legal-he: Free legal information for Floridians on evictions, foreclosures, family law, public benefits, and debt, with a search tool that connects you to legal aid providers by location and topic. Available in English, Spanish, and Haitian Creole.
unemployment-insurance-new-jersey: Temporary weekly payments if you lost work through no fault of your own, from the New Jersey Department of Labor. File online any time at myunemployment.nj.gov, or by phone through a Reemployment Call Center: North Jersey 201-601-4100, Central Jersey 732-761-2020, South Jersey 856-507-2340. Call centers are open Monday through Friday.
wv-chip-childrens-health-insurance-progr: WV CHIP covers children and pregnant women in working families who have no other health insurance and earn too much for Medicaid. It covers checkups, dental, vision, prescriptions, and more with low or no cost to the family. Apply through wvPATH along with Medicaid at wvpath.wv.gov, and call the WVCHIP Helpline at 1-877-982-2447 (1-877-WVA-CHIP) with questions.
